Friend,

I grew up on the west side of Winston-Salem, the youngest of five, watching my parents give everything they had to this state and the people in it. I never imagined that decades later, North Carolina would be the place deciding the fate of the entire Congress. _But here we are._

**Everything comes down to North Carolina.**

_The House.
The Senate.
Whether the Radical Left gets free rein to ram through their agenda, unchecked._

Republicans have a $600 million advantage heading into these midterms, and outside groups are pouring money into races across the country (including here in Minnesota!). But I'd rather run a grassroots campaign and win on the strength of our community than take corporate money and compromise on who or what I'm fighting for. We are just hours away from our last end-of-quarter FEC deadline before Election Day. If you've been looking for a moment to chip in, this is it. Every dollar you give goes directly toward the work that wins elections – knocking doors, reaching voters, and making sure MN-03 stays blue in November. Will you chip in before midnight? I am counting on your support today to help me campaign for Democrats across the country.

Peter -
Today. Not tomorrow. Not next week.
Today is the day I need you to donate to my PAC, Fight for the People.
I am doing everything I can to speak out and raise money for Democrats before the midterm elections. I am traveling to Michigan, Georgia, and more battleground races across the nation to help us turn out in numbers too big to rig.
**[Right now, I am asking you to support that work by making a donation. Here’s why:**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kdh-fftp-em?refcode=em260930-exp&refcode2=1377_2563979_1w4NXi&akid=1377%2E2563979%2E1w4NXi)
Tonight, our last end-of-quarter deadline of the midterms comes to a close.
When tonight’s deadline passes, exactly how much the PAC has raised to fund this critical work will become public. Everyone will be looking at this report to see if I still have the grassroots support that has powered me through my career.
I’ve held many titles in my life: District Attorney. Attorney General. U.S. Senator, Vice President.
Even, as you may know, Big Sister General.
But for me, it’s never been about the title. It’s about the work. And in the run up to these midterms, doing the work takes resources.
Millions of people donated to my campaign last election. You have stood with me when I needed you most, and it meant the world to me.
If you can make a contribution of $5 — or whatever you can afford today — I will put those resources to work immediately to help elect Democrats across the country.
**So what do you say, Peter? I am counting on your support today. Together, we will show everyone watching that we are ready to overwhelmingly elect leaders who will fight for the people this November.**

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football’s 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville’s time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year’s Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP’s SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul “Bear” Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? _

Tonight at midnight is our end-of-quarter deadline. It's the last one before Election Day, and it's the last quarterly public report voters, the media, and my opponent will see before ballots are cast. My Democrat opponent, Annie Andrews, and her liberal super PACs have raised over $20 million to defeat me. That money is already flooding South Carolina airwaves, trying to hide her radical agenda from voters. The Special and Runoff elections were expensive. We put every dollar we raised into winning. _**Brad Hicks**_

| | Hello Peter,

I am so grateful to share some wonderful news. Thanks to you, we have reached our quarterly fundraising goal, and we finished **$78 over goal**.
Every dollar in that total came from someone who decided that Ohio's 8th District deserves a representative who listens, shows up, and works for the families who call this place home. Whether you gave $5 or $500, shared a post, knocked on a door, or simply spoke up for this campaign in your circle, you made this happen.
That extra $78 may look small on paper, but to me it means people kept stepping forward even after we crossed the line. That is the kind of energy that wins campaigns and builds stronger communities.
Your support goes straight to the ground game: reaching voters, organizing neighborhoods, and making sure every corner of OH-08 hears our message of opportunity, dignity, and results.
We still have important work ahead, and I'm excited to keep doing it alongside you. Thank you for believing in this campaign and in what we can build together.
With deep gratitude,
Dr. Vanessa Enoch
Democratic Candidate for Congress, Ohio's 8th District

name: Aaron Ford
subject: Bear with me
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
I know it’s getting late, but please bear with me for a moment.
Nate Silver, one of the best election forecasters out there, made a list of the most competitive governors’ races in the country. Guess who was at the very top?
**Nevada.**
Look, we knew our race would be a toss-up. But being the MOST competitive one this cycle? That's a lot of pressure. I won't pretend it isn't.
But that’s the deck we were dealt, and we have to fight with everything we’ve got to win.
**Tonight marks our last end-of-quarter deadline of the election cycle.** After that, it’s a sprint to November 3.
The money we raise right now will be put toward keeping our ads up and fueling our get-out-the-vote efforts.
MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo and his special interest backers are outspending us. But if enough members of this team step up tonight, that won't matter — we'll out-organize their millions.
**_So please, if you can chip in before midnight, it’d be a huge help. Can I count on your $5 donation?_**

body:
# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=2979%2E5691347%2EF1HqWs)

Peter,
First of all, I want to say thank you.
Let me explain why:
This campaign has raised an extraordinary amount of money from an extraordinary number of people giving small-dollar, grassroots donations. That grassroots support is something that I’m grateful for every day. I promise you, Peter: _I never, ever take you or your support for granted._
But the reality is that even with that unprecedented level of grassroots support, we still have critical fundraising goals to meet in the final stretch of this campaign to build the resources it’ll take to win here in Georgia.
The Senate GOP’s main Super PAC — which is just one of many right-wing Super PACs who could spend money on this race — has raised more than $500 million. And then there’s still Trump and his Super PAC, plus other far-right billionaires like Elon Musk waiting in the wings.
The truth is that MAGA can spend endlessly attacking us because they’ve got an army of billionaires and corporate PAC donors lining up to fund the smears.
_We expect to be outspent in this race,_ possibly by hundreds of millions of dollars. We don’t need to match the Super PACs dollar for dollar, but we do need to make sure we get our message out.
So please, I’m humbly asking:
[**Can you give $5 to my reelection campaign today to help me fight back against the dark money Super PACs who are going to flood Georgia with attacks? Donate today to fight their lies with the TRUTH >>>**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261001-1-f&utm_campaign=em261001-1-f&t=2&akid=2979%2E5691347%2EF1HqWs)
_Post-Citizens United_ , Super PACs and secret money in politics are totally out of control, corrupting policymaking on behalf of the rich and powerful.
And when members of Congress aren't fundraising from lobbyists and corporate PACs, they're just trying to dodge getting bombed by these Super PACs.
Candidates all over the country are facing down hundreds of millions in Super PAC spending from dark-money groups that don’t even disclose their donors until after the election, if ever.
Is this the way we want our government to work? Do we really want to allow unlimited, secret political money to bend the nation’s agenda in darkness?
Peter: All across Georgia and all across the country, a wave is building. The kind of wave that comes once a generation, when the people have been pushed too far and decide all together, all at once: **enough is enough.**
That is the message that we’re going to send when we WIN this November.
Yes, this election will be tough.
But I know how to win tough fights. I’ve done it before.
Let’s do it again.
[**Please, consider making a donation to my reelection campaign today. I wouldn’t ask if it didn’t make a real difference, Peter.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261001-1-f&utm_campaign=em261001-1-f&t=3&akid=2979%2E5691347%2EF1HqWs)
Thank you, sincerely, for chipping in if you can and for everything you do to support this campaign and this movement.
As always,
Jon

body:
...but you deserve full transparency.
#

Hi Team --
This wasn’t the email we were hoping to send today, but as a top supporter to GIFFORDS, you deserve full transparency.
Last night we closed the books on our September fundraising deadline — the last one before early voting kicks off for the midterm elections.
Unfortunately, as hard as we tried, we fell short of our ambitious FEC goal.
Look, we’re not going to pretend the sky is falling because we missed this goal. We’re also not going to lie and say there’s a “RARE 2X MATCH OFFER!!!” You deserve better than the scammy tactics that organizations use to scare you into donating.
**But here is the truth: This puts an unexpected gap in our budget.**
We’ve carefully built this budget so we can spend as much as possible to help our candidates win in November. These are races that could be decided by just a handful of votes, and our impact could mean the difference between victory and defeat.
But if we don’t fill this budget gap, then we’ll be forced to make some tough decisions about where we can no longer afford to invest. That means we’ll reach far fewer voters than we hoped, which would hand a massive gift to the gun lobby.
As you can probably expect, that is the last possible thing we want to do...which is why we are reaching out to you as a last resort:
**[If there is anything you can spare, we hope you’ll consider standing with Gabby and contributing to GIFFORDS PAC today. Your donation will help us fully fund our voter outreach programs and will be immediately put to work fighting back against the gun lobby’s attacks.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261001-1-b&t=1&akid=11886%2E3935704%2E3A4gZi)

## Co-Pilot Tried to Crash Israel Flight
The co-pilot of a Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight stabbed the captain and [tried to crash](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp_GdEb28JNQuNiGLttuiQZ7HGavgciegPL2V7l5hFt_0tF3zr_bdENOvN3_4kpO4j5tdJZEIpQnLhkpxcT3RVAE_ReFZ0mEExjotTXa2Am98EFTi1VwkQioqcjZy2Cu7WAbWy0uxmEAa-boB981c4Aeu77t2z5C11jEit2bZ42x1pgOhhrQUGx9uM4Rmosn1RoKLHuu_--8yUIxvfaDcu33tUpuEXkU1fxRMCoYz_Os_Tb796hgfKMVjGZQMDZGwfix0h8tHfigLBR0wWdgjRlnRj1nPJN-cNql6Jhe4Tkj14usqcouPE5OiUt_Ua25r8jp54f8Mt_h4DsAAP__cH-FWQ) the plane Wednesday morning, Israeli officials said, until passengers broke into the cockpit and subdued him. More than 170 Israelis were aboard. Flight-tracking data showed the jet dropped over 14,000 feet in under 30 seconds. The wounded captain, lying on the floor and covered in blood, reached up and released the cockpit door lock, a spokesman for the prime minister told the media. A second set of pilots on board, due to relieve the first pair, [landed the jet](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE8DmVHbGBgCB5uQzaYbosZuQ-8aGJke0Nx-xf9H-GmVVKr3_jzHJ3Libf6NKzmJ-7jRdSQSoTzykZFSTDwvgiLo_1F4H4lwNGBapUGBHtELnzRaLIOLRIbqkpzuenjYXte6XFwXe4LOtI2N_UR98J0Nk8WuCbVtGgslu3tPA2gN0Ji-MggUrQ-PKZq681RYoMCy5-rvzpssFNNnPylXfl_L5BaR11HUvwozFGa4rqvaJn9z3P2d7DmFwgwrh5BIER5SmOGbS4X3hKyEksKTTxX4pCwUFK2UZ9r8R2GiLCr7DVuA1jzK7MLr4pT4aLvCwrwip68r8kODpzP_AwAA__8eroep) at Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where both pilots were hospitalized. Passengers reached Israel on a replacement aircraft after eight hours on the ground. Saudi authorities are holding the co-pilot, and Israel ordered identity checks on every pilot flying into the country. One passenger who helped stop the attack was still in his [bloodstained shirt](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAQhp8Gd6wAc2u7cJGG7tKmtGZhsOcOgwWzu_LbR06KPEDqmf-Tvu_X5_IJlCivP2HHmWNZMr5bQmasC7UKmGKidWNgBv-N4dkSwmKUuUutpNILeKYXLha6MEdEg32Hsx4mNdpJ97rbZn8fRwweovZgvR5sP-JoJmvj8AE6TB3NF08rpbVSH2a6GVAYrQ_jI5p-8CiswkBc6u2rUOYNYzrLC-vNl71L88Z8NNH_EMYJ4_J5lMbXSRh3gYVxahLG9UoY9y41BXlJCuNiOsPzASQPaA3zilU2ppSkv-gYJGX5SKUEuSNykxkZ8gnbU0L7t2kSaqUXXt9_k0mIjFVu9AX-m_IqgRn3g4VxXZ3D8aaUqN0HYdW6A6U_Hvyf-V-z-R0AAP__u72dwQ) when he met Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The airline warned against "premature speculation" about a motive.
## Trump, AI CEOs Sign Safety Accord
President Trump and the heads of the country's largest artificial intelligence companies signed a one-page [safety accord](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnDAQhJ8GOiPb-OegcJGG7tKmRHvLcmxibGQvkHv7iLzC3400mk8z8-s5PYEDx_dP2MjLkqZIVwkkQnnikoHCEvi9CogA_qH5KIFgstp2ymilzQQofNLkoJ79QmSprcmbx6B7N5jW1KunvkOjje5mIIcdaHSmN1_d8MJ2MA5r9jfPaG2M1l92aCxoWhzO_Wux7QOpcppmlpSb34mjrLSETzopN5i2OvhVZC9V-6OyY2XH67oafJV7x-1XdrxlZUfJx7YrYIUpFmE5hFNUQrgq-ktYVNopAiuIsua0M6ozhSMK5M8dkZzCjamzn_eLQ-DSPSqn3xtw-N9Evnng6e2_AAAA__9dzYke) at the White House on Tuesday. He called it "morally binding" and "almost like a constitution," and said the industry is policing itself. The companies agreed to [four layers of controls](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO4yAQxvGnsbtEw4CDXVCcdHKXq0660prAEHOLjQWTRPv2q-wrbPt90q_4_7suV0o57fc_tLGTWJadXy2zCNcltUqcY073VUiE_AeHR8tMCwJeTgpOoBbykp68GOqDi8zIumen7ASjmZRW_eqixzjxhOCjJRx80OMINzWSDkFFa_vk3p4CUApgwOmMBByND-MtoraeOwMckpR6_l_SLivH_FmeXM--bH12q8jROv2rw7nDWepD1lZ8ovz-36OBypR_l51y-Fsf29HhfJQmrcNZKauHi9GD1ZPROA3YVxeOV8o5tYvtDNw3St9ULz8s9HT4FQAA__8P93mp) and audits, including internal evaluations, an outside auditor, and review by each company's board. The text says it may make sense to codify the steps into law later. It follows months of safety failures, including models that gained unauthorized access to other companies' systems. Trump also signed an order telling the federal government to say "Super Intelligence" instead of AI, and said he will name a czar for AI within days. The accord carries no enforcement mechanism. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who has pushed to slow development, called the agreement only "[a start](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGu2zAQRE9DdTTIlWJJBQs36n6AFEGQSliTS2sTijTItYV_-0C5wq9nMJj3fn2sH8iJ8-M77uQkljXT0RKJUF25VaQUEz82QRH0fym8WiJcwcBVW6ONXdELv2kdsAsuEgH1HTk7zmYaZtvbbnM9mTGitQbwPg5TP9mAeB0RzX2c5hk6dueeNcZaY77BfAE0FAcfpnuEfvSkBkOBpdTLn8JZNorps7ypXnzZu-Q2kWdT_U3BomA5juOyt3xmChbK-tUULCeWgqXIRlXBIvW1P3XTyNqX3ITlJVyy9rUcuemAn7pEjd5ToorC-aFxv_PZUbBg1bcbhPjj98-uuvA8OCVu11EN5rEjp_-_5Is63w7-BQAA___bmYwp)."
## Last US Troops Leave Iraq after 12 Years
U.S. Central Command said Wednesday it had completed an "[orderly withdrawal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2u3CAYRVeDO0aA_fxTUESKLKV4aVNan-EyJmGMA9944t1Hky2kvtLVOefH5_JJMcX9_p0esBzysuNVE5hRllgLIYUU7xsTM7lf8M-aQItRppdaSaUXchxPLB013gbAoG1g9TCpsZt0q5vNDugnB-MVnNejcwgf07iO2g8r6TCtTbTvP62U1kp9mOlmSCF0zo9rMO3gIDoFHzmX288cd94Q0pVPlJvLjybZjfmoov0izCzMTKt7O7w3YeZvO6PsxDHvlISZn1VyyfmoEn8OOIaXCXRCxkK_5Qt-R_V0SW3kBSrCzJVzuUQ7Ry_ar7rtx0GP_dQU649XTCnWfhCduj8opn88_J8ZT2v-BgAA__-MLIki)" of American troops from Iraq, ending a mission that began in 2014 against ISIS. About 2,500 troops had been stationed there for years. It's the second time the U.S. has pulled every soldier out. The first came in 2011, eight years after the 2003 invasion. Forces returned when ISIS seized much of Syria and northern Iraq and pushed toward Baghdad. Roughly 4,500 American service members died across the two decades, most of them between 2003 and 2011. The [withdrawal was negotiated](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u2zAMRp9G3hhIlPI3aMhidLldOxqsTMVsFSuVeGOkT1-4r3DnDzj4zvnxMX2QFFnv3-nBUXOdVt56YVVuk_RGXHKR-6KkSuk3z5-9ME1o8QTOgnUTJZUXT4GGOWZmZD9wdOervYSr825Y4jUHSseUMTjyNpyyTewu_hhme_TB-0HiznPWOmftEa8HJMs5pPnyM6M_JzbB8ixa2-FXlVUXzuVdX9wOqT6GEhfVZzf-ZnA0OG7bdnj0dd8MjryCrAbHXcvgWHXhZnD87KCt1meHzgpaoTC9GKTRH6Cs3MAhvJka5N0e6E6ydgXp0qHxszbdcdTgdsM5f_tLQ4vzc5NSpJ_OJtj7g6T8P6hf7PqK-C8AAP__O-COjw) in 2024 and kept on schedule by the current administration, with Sept. 30 as the deadline. The remaining anti-ISIS mission moves to Jordan. Iraq's prime minister marked the departure with a ceremony, and his government has pushed its deadline to disarm Iranian-backed militias to June 2027.

Good morning, friends! I wanted to share a few thoughts before I dive into my day.
I try to start every day with a morning walk. I live where neighborhoods start turning into pastures, and my morning walk is the one time in my day when I can really appreciate the world around me: the birds singing, the flowers blooming, the horses grazing.
**My morning routine keeps me grounded, helps me prepare for long days on the campaign trail and reminds me of everything we 're fighting for.**
I think about the work we can do to make life better for Kansans and folks across the country. I think about fighting for our values -- not Republican or Democratic values but _American_ values like honesty, kindness and compassion. I think about ending the chaos and corruption that have run rampant in Washington, D.C., for far too long.
This time of year the mornings are cooling down and I'm also reminded that Election Day is drawing near. Save the date if you haven't already -- it's Nov. 3, just a little over four weeks away. That means we have four weeks left to hold on to our narrow lead, reach undecided Kansas voters and defeat Sen. Roger Marshall.
And early voting starts in just 13 days. If you're in Kansas, make sure you have a plan in place to vote. You can find more information [here](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a025b767-c79b-4e32-85a4-b0dc9745ee6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
After last night's big FEC deadline, I'm feeling extra appreciation for all our supporters, from those who have been with us from the very beginning of this campaign, to those who just heard about all our momentum in Kansas and decided to get involved, to people like you reading these words.
It's still early as I write this, so it'll be a bit before we're finished tallying the final numbers on the end-of-quarter goal we've been talking so much about, but I am feeling hopeful and inspired by all the grassroots donations we've received. I know that we did everything we could ahead of this critical moment in our campaign, and I feel good about that.
**That 's how I want all of us to feel on Election Day, too. I want us to know we left it all on the field. And that evening when the news breaks that a Democrat has won in Kansas for the first time in nearly a hundred years, I want you to know that you made that happen.**
With the resources we've raised from thousands of grassroots donors like you (and those that are still coming in), we can get even more ads on TV and radio, more letters in mailboxes and more signs in people's yards. We can keep up the phone banks and canvassing, and I can keep traveling all over the state sharing our message with Kansans.
I feel confident that if we can keep all that up, we can really win this race. **[That's why we ask for your support -- because it absolutely will be the difference between a history-making win and a heartbreaking loss that keeps Roger Marshall in the Senate supporting bad policies that hurt our families.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1e328e71-3539-4017-bfe2-6ee4242f9037?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Thank you for all you're doing to help create real change in Washington.
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1e328e71-3539-4017-bfe2-6ee4242f9037?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
With hope and gratitude,
Adam

Maine's next governor will inherit the largest budget crisis in state history, thanks largely to poor fiscal management by Gov. Janet Mills (D), Maine Democratic lawmakers, and worse-than-expected economic forecasts released Wednesday.
The state's Sept. 30 forecast projects a $1.085 billion gap in the General Fund, which pays for schools, health care and most state operations. Roads face another $256.7 million gap. Those shortages cover the two-year budget beginning July 1, 2027.
The harsh reality is that Augusta has only limited tools for resolving the financial crisis: raising taxes (again) or cutting spending -- which would be anathema to the Portland-area Democrats who currently control the State House.
This Substack is reader-supported. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..c08sqr5dSOTudMfTzB1f1IWvYQAgnZY1Bh3HOYpAo_8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=218321968)
The budget office explains the problem plainly: "One-time transfers and financing measures support the near-term budget but do not address these recurring gaps."
By "recurring gaps" the budget offices means the utter inability to fund Democrat wishlist policies on permanent basis unless the governor is hiding a pot of gold somewhere in the Blaine House.
The budget catastrophe is a sharp contrast from the tight fiscal ship Gov. Mills and the Democratic majority inherited.
General Fund spending approved for the current two-year budget totals $12 billion. The final budget under Republican Gov. Paul LePage totaled $7.215 billion. Democrats have added $4.785 billion, a 66.3% increase before inflation. The forecast calls for another $1.256 billion in spending in the next budget. Available resources grow just $322.4 million.
Mills would leave a projected $13.256 billion in General Fund appropriations, 83.7% above LePage's final two-year total.
The current General Fund plan ends with a projected $2.4 million balance against $12 billion in spending. That is two-hundredths of 1%. The Highway Fund finishes with $930,812. These are budget balances, separate from the state's rainy-day reserves.
Democrats have already approved dipping into those reserves. As the Maine Wire reported in July, the supplemental budget authorized roughly $292 million in withdrawals, including $155.2 million for one-time $300 checks -- checks which have been documented going out to foreign nationals and even dead people.
Much like orbital mechanics can predict the collision of celestial objects thousands of years before cosmic fireworks, the slow-motion fiscal train wreck is not a surprise for those who paid attention to the trajectory of state spending and revenue.
In October 2024, The Maine Wire reported a projected $949.2 million combined General Fund and Highway Fund gap for the budget that is now underway.
The Legislature subsequently balanced that budget by raising taxes on working Mainers in the form of new taxes on Netflix, higher tobacco taxes, higher taxes on recreational cannabis (in legal markets) and a so called "millionaire's tax."
The Legislature suspended the state's spending limit for both current budget years. An April 10 legislative summary put appropriations $159.3 million above the calculated limit for fiscal 2026 and $191.2 million above it for fiscal 2027.
None of that is enough to keep up with the drunken-sailor-in-Bangkok spending to which Democratic lawmakers have committed future taxpayers.
Tax collections have slowed somewhat compared with the state's spending commitments, but t have not collapsed.
General Fund revenue actually rose 2.5% in the fiscal year that ended June 30 and exceeded the budget estimate. Yet the new forecast still shows a billion-dollar General Fund gap ahead -- a statement as to just how unbridled Democrat spending was in the last legislative session compared to the actual resources available.
The largest drivers of the massive shortfall are predictable: Medicaid, a program rife with unchecked fraud -- largely committed by foreign nationals, migrants, and so-called asylum seekers -- and rising school budgets that commit the state to parallel funding increases due to the constitutional obligation that the state pick up 55% of the local education tab.

Health and Human Services appropriations rise $612.1 million to $5.154 billion in the next two-year General Fund projection. Education adds $417.5 million. Together, those policy areas account for about 82% of the $1.256 billion spending increase.
Within MaineCare, the forecast names $345 million in added costs for residential services, home- and community-based care, hospitals and federally required drug coverage. It separately identifies $29.8 million for the state's Medicare Part D obligation and $20.6 million from a higher state Medicaid matching share.
The principal Section 21 account is the $595.2 million developmental-services waiver line. Section 29's supports waiver accounts for $139 million. These are state General Fund amounts, excluding federal matching dollars. The eight-account subtotal also includes community and children's mental-health Medicaid accounts, developmental Medicaid services and behavioral-health Medicaid seed funding.
The state's commitment to fund 55% of Essential Programs and Services for public schools requires another $280.7 million in the next budget. General Purpose Aid rises $349 million overall, from $3.046 billion to $3.395 billion. The broader education policy area reaches $5.227 billion.
Department of Education expenditure reports show district general-fund spending rose $215.9 million, or 6.9%, between fiscal 2024 and 2025, reaching $3.339 billion, with Lewiston and Portland leading the way with the largest increases.

The forecast includes "the full-year cost of programs, rates and other requirements phased in during the 2026-2027 biennium." It describes adjustments for "known or predictable changes."
Acting State Budget Officer Kimberly Smith cautioned that obligations have historically been "modified, deferred, or funded below statutory levels with legislative approval." The gaps therefore are projections under current assumptions, rather than definitive shortfalls in a budget the next Legislature has yet to enact.
"Closing the projected 2028-2029 gaps will require recurring revenue, sustainable expenditure changes or a combination of both," the budget office wrote.

Those shortages cover the two-year budget beginning July 1, 2027. Sometimes I get asked what seems like a simple question: "What's the hardest part of running for Congress?"
There are a lot of obvious answers. The hours aren't great. Generally, we're talking 10 hours a day when I'm home and as many as 18 hours when we're on the road... but I don't mind it that much.
Then there are the speeches. I give four or five a week. Most run ten to fifteen minutes. I don't write them down, and they change each time I give them, so I don't get bored.
Then there's meeting hundreds of people every week... oh wait, that's probably the best part.
Some days I spend four to six hours in my truck, driving, but these eleven counties are truly beautiful. I can't complain about that.
If those aren't the hardest part, what is? ...

Events: We're a grassroots campaign, so we need to meet people face-to-face. If you're having a fall festival, food truck event, flea market, farmers market, or art fair, let us know.

---

---

You’ve offered your time and effort to our campaign. Offering the full, unvarnished truth is the least I can do. And the cold, hard truth? _We fell short of our End-of-Quarter fundraising goal last night._ We have never fallen short of a major fundraising goal throughout this reelection campaign. # Update from the Campaign Trail - September 2026
---
## Team Turner is Building Momentum as We Head into the Home Stretch
---
Friends,Only 5 days remain before early voting begins and there are just 34 days until Election Day.Team Turner is working hard to ensure we leave it all on the field and remind voters of the great things we have been able to achieve together.Read on and learn more in this update from the campaign trail.

---

---
###

### U.S Chamber of Commerce Endorsement
---
As a part of their Free Enterprise Express Opportunity Tour, the U.S Chamber of Commerce recently endorsed our campaign for re-election."The U.S. Chamber of Commerce is proud to be in Dayton today to show our support for Congressman Mike Turner and endorse him for reelection to represent Ohio's Tenth Congressional District," said Tom Sullivan, Senior Vice President of Small Business Policy at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. "Congressman Turner is a dedicated public servant who supports free enterprise policies that make Ohio's small businesses, workers, and families stronger. The Chamber is very proud to support his reelection, and we look forward to continuing to work with him in the 120th Congress.".You can read more [here.](https://click-493811.icptrack.com/icp/relay.php?r=126057447&msgid=1044533&act=NE1B&c=493811&pid=12637504&destination=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.uschamber.com%2Fimproving-government%2Fu-s-chamber-endorses-rep-mike-turner-for-ohios-tenth-district-on-national-free-enterprise-express-opportunity-tour%3Futm_id%3D97757_v0_s00_e0_tv2_a1demo0gzr3ws4%26fbclid%3DIwY2xjawUpCUpleHRuA2FlbQIxMQBwZG9mAXNydGMGYXBwX2lkEDIyMjAzOTE3ODgyMDA4OTIAAR4926z2QYl90FqHpDFfnQQNig-hiD-mZf2lFJYVlYOWH3XKCKO9zLmUuM8MKA_aem_90X9GN87b2D0XZNNTfIHfQ&cf=64880&v=8796a5248d33c9feee9a85a175292e8e0491e309d189a06aa7b7a835ddedd4b3)

### New Ad Launch - "Delievered"
---
Earlier this month, we launched a strong new message to the voters of Ohio's 10th Congressional district - "Delivered".The message is simple; when it comes to the issues that matter most, Mike Turner delivers. Whether it's jobs, healthcare, pensions, or making our communities safer, Mike Turner fights for us and gets things done.
---
| [](https://click-493811.icptrack.com/icp/relay.php?r=126057447&msgid=1044533&act=NE1B&c=493811&pid=12637504&destination=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3D_9rnwVND3vM&cf=64880&v=21644434a9187b2188daa4a9f370ca8f1f5820857923bef81ecb7329d01b263e)

Please share this ad with your friends and families to remind others that there's too much at stake in this Election. Make a plan to vote Mike Turner for Congress, and encourage your friends and families to do the same.

---

###

### Knocking Doors
---
Throughout the month of September, I have been working hard knocking doors throughout the district. I've been talking to voters about the issues that affect them and our community most. We'll keep knocking, keep listening, and keep building on the incredible support we're seeing.

Earlier this month, we held a campaign fundraiser and rally at the iconic barn of Matt and Keri Miller. This event was a wonderful opportunity to connect with so many friends and supporters in Greene County! Thank you again to the Millers for hosting as well as Marilyn Reid for helping organize!

In early July, roughly 5,800 delegates to the National Education Association's Representative Assembly gathered to choose a successor to Becky Pringle, termed out after six years as president of the country's largest labor union. They chose Princess Moss, a career union officer and elementary music teacher from rural Louisa County, Virginia, who now leads the NEA's 2.8 million members. She won with 50.3 percent of the vote -- half a point clear of a runoff. Half the assembly voted for someone else.
Hold on to that number. It is the most honest thing anyone said all week, and it came from the union's own members.
Albert Shanker, the late president of the American Federation of Teachers, is famously credited with the line that explains the modern teachers' union: "When schoolchildren start paying union dues, that's when I'll start representing the interests of schoolchildren." Shanker's defenders dispute that he ever said it -- the Albert Shanker Institute has hunted for a source and come up empty -- and argue he said something blunter and no better: "I don't represent children. I represent teachers." Disputed or not, six years of Becky Pringle's NEA ran the experiment for him.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/30637ff7-7c18-4117-ac25-85b65a1512bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Consider the ledger she leaves behind. Pringle took the NEA's helm in the fall of 2020, as classrooms sat locked down. Last September, the federal government released the final round of post-pandemic Nation's Report Card data: twelfth-grade math and reading scores had fallen three points since 2019, to their lowest levels in decades -- by some measures the lowest ever recorded -- and eighth-grade science had dropped four points. The steepest losses were concentrated among the weakest students, so the gap the union claims to exist to close widened under the union's watch. The seniors who took that test were freshmen when union leaders were still pressing to hold classrooms closed into the fall of 2020.
While scores fell, the checks kept moving. The NEA reported about $391 million in dues revenue in 2025. Its political arm, the NEA Advocacy Fund, raised nearly $27 million for the 2024 cycle -- virtually all of it aimed at electing Kamala Harris and more Democrats to the House and Senate. In recent cycles roughly 98 percent of the union's federal contributions have gone to Democrats. This past year it spent more than $51 million on political activity and lobbying, and gave $5,000 apiece to each of the sixteen Democrats on the House education committee -- and not a dollar to any Republican. Members' dues bought a party, not a pedagogy.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e34c326c-607c-4444-a74e-935576444b93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Pringle herself collected roughly half a million dollars a year, while the NEA's own website describes her -- apparently without irony -- as a "fierce social justice warrior." Her final-year manifesto was headlined "We're Not Done Yet." That part is true, though not in the way she meant.
Enter Moss. Her campaign video announced that "this campaign is about organizing, mobilizing." In her speech before the vote, she called on the NEA's 2.8 million members to throw themselves into ongoing organizing -- for education and, pointedly, workforce issues. Not phonics. Not tutoring. Not a syllable about the report card. Her ascent -- student member, local leader, state president, NEA vice president, NEA president -- is a triumph of the union's institutional ladder, climbed rung by rung over three decades, and it rewarded, as such ladders always do, the person who knows the machine best.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/99866ac8-13b7-4984-9540-e3a9e6797283?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Her victory statement offered the familiar chord progression: "when we invest in public education, we invest in the future of every student." As longtime union watcher Larry Sand put it after the election, borrowing from the Who: "Meet the new boss, same as the old boss."
What does the 50.3 percent tell us? The delegates know the union best. They see the dues statements, the shrinking rolls -- membership is down to 2.8 million -- and the political apparatus that consumes the difference. Even inside the machine, nearly half of them wanted something other than the Pringle era's third term of itself. What they got instead was continuity: more organizing, more mobilizing, more Democratic check-writing. The children -- who pay no dues, cast no votes, and fund no PACs -- will keep receiving exactly the representation their balance sheet says they're worth.
Shanker's line survives, disputed or not, because two generations of report cards keep confirming it. If Moss wants a legacy better than her predecessor's, the path is obvious and, inside her union, all but impossible: spend the members' money on the members' classrooms, and measure success in reading scores instead of Senate seats. Don't bet on it. The schoolchildren have never paid dues. Until they do, they'll keep sending in their report cards -- and the union will keep sending in the checks.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b4b18219-d104-4386-b4bf-908b11ee0f8d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Marshall’s watch, 63,000 Kansans are on track to lose their health insurance, gas is over a dollar more than it was a year ago, diesel is at record highs and 700 farms in Kansas closed last year. We simply cannot afford to have another six years of leadership that is so out of touch.= | | = Adam has talked to Kansans whose businesses have been hurt by the disastrous tariffs and forever wars that are raising the cost of everyday goods. He has heard from families worried about affording healthcare and getting food on the table. He has listened to hundreds of Kansans who are ready for something different. That’s why Adam is running — and why this campaign is powered by over 50,000 grassroots supporters who believe in a better future for Kansas and this country. Adam is ready to fight to lower the cost of gas, groceries and healthcare, and end the partisan chaos in Washington. But Sen. Marshall’s allies have now spent more than $7 million to attack this campaign on the airwaves. They’re terrified of our momentum and will spend whatever it takes to drown us out. But we have something more powerful on our side: a grassroots team of folks like you,= That’s why we’re leading in the polls by a narrow margin and why elections experts, including Nate Silver and even Fox News, have upgraded this race — and Real Clear Polling just shifted our race to a toss-up! = If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | = Thank you for being one of the 50,000 folks powering this movement. — Team Hamilton | Adam Hamilton is a husband, father, pastor and fifth-generation Kansan. Now, he’s running for U.S. Senate as an independent-minded Democrat. Just like you, he’s tired of the chaos and corruption in Washington that is harming our farmers, raising costs at the checkout line and making critical health care services unattainable. He hears your concerns and is ready to get to work for you. Early polling shows Adam neck-and-neck in this race, and with your help, we can win big this November. = | | = | | = | This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com Rather donate by check or by mail You can mail checks to, Hamilton for Kansas PO Box 6 Stilwell, KS 66085. **Thursday, October 1, 2026 -**_****_
**Iran** : Iranian President says Tehran will pursue U.S. dialogue. Tehran rejects report U.S. ordered its UN delegation to leave New York. UK says there are "strong indications" Iran played role in RAF Fairford incident. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims six militants killed in southeastern Iran.
**Yemen** : Saudi-backed forces, Ansarallah report strikes in Taiz and Saada.
**Palestine** : Israeli attacks continue as 105 bodies recovered from Gaza City rubble are buried. Israeli strike kills Palestinian journalist in Gaza, bringing journalist death toll to 263. Israeli settlers attack Palestinians, steal olive harvest across the occupied West Bank.
**Lebanon** : Israeli attacks continue across south Lebanon despite U.S.-brokered agreement. Lebanon documents suspected Israeli war crimes. Syria and Hezbollah hold first known face-to-face talks in Turkey.
**U.S.** :**** U.S. economy grew 2.2% in Q2, upgraded from earlier estimate. Tennessee botches second execution this year, governor halts all remaining 2026 executions. War Secretary Pete Hegseth announces new drone command, 20 percent cut to generals in "State of the Force" speech. Federal Trade Commission launches investigation into OpenAI, Anthropic over AI safety. ICE briefly published, then removed, internal reports showing medical failures in 33 detainee deaths. Department of Justice files ethics complaint against nearly all Minnesota federal judges over immigration-surge comments. Senate confirms Keith Sonderling as Labor Secretary. Sen. Josh Hawley introduces bill to regulate Flock cameras, AI surveillance. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reports over $250 million in income from 2025. Judge rules U.S. can deport Milwaukee Muslim leader on national security grounds. South Africa summons U.S. Ambassador for third time over "undiplomatic conduct." French court sentences 13 to prison over 2021 Channel crossing that killed 31 migrants.
**International** :**** Bolivian attorney general detained days after U.S. revoked his visa over alleged drug trafficking ties. Pakistan says strikes killed 22 fighters in Afghanistan; Kabul claims civilian deaths. Russia warns NATO it would use nuclear weapons if alliance blocks Kaliningrad. Brazil briefs French, German officials on alleged U.S. and Russian election interference. Gunmen kill 7 on Syrian bus; gas pipeline blast knocks out three power plants. Iraqi armed group suspends military operations after U.S. troop withdrawal. China builds new military facility in Laos, possibly first full People's Liberation Army base in Southeast Asia. Norway's parliament probes Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre, 10 others over links to Jeffrey Epstein. Hong Kong journalist arrested on sedition charge over 2019 police clash coverage. MI5 warns UK academics to sever ties with Chinese research group over alleged spying. Rwanda open to hosting EU migrant transfer facilities, lawmakers say. Entire newsroom arrested in Egypt in significant press crackdown.

* * *
# Iran
* **Iranian President says Tehran will pursue U.S. dialogue:** Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran would continue pursuing dialogue with the United States despite repeated attacks during negotiations. "We have never avoided dialogue and will not do so, although the United States targeted our country three times," Pezeshkian said, adding that Iran was also seeking to expand land-based trade with Pakistan, Iraq, Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan amid "restrictions at sea."
* Separately, President Donald Trump [told](https://substack.com/redirect/3707a61c-a8b4-45a0-977c-035ddd07a3f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Time that Iran had made an offer concerning reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but said what he had seen was "simply not enough." Trump said renewed U.S. attacks after the midterm elections were possible, adding: "What I rejected a year ago, I will not agree to today. Iran could be destroyed, and that's possible."
* **Tehran rejects report U.S. ordered its UN delegation to leave New York:** Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and the Iranian delegation [left](https://substack.com/redirect/17c47092-3a1f-4751-80ff-4b5f4dae5d0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) New York on Monday evening according to a prearranged schedule that had been communicated to the U.S. State Department on September 17, Iran's UN mission said.
* The statement came after Axios, citing a source, reported that the U.S. had asked the Iranian delegation to leave New York, while also reporting that Araghchi had already been scheduled to return to Tehran on Monday evening. Iran's mission called the claim "baseless and worthless."
* **UK says there are "strong indications" Iran played role in RAF Fairford incident:** The government [believes](https://substack.com/redirect/8d8c6550-b784-4ead-8e97-4c83a36922a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran played a role in an incident at RAF Fairford that led to the arrest of five UK nationals, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, but provided no further details or evidence for the claim.
* Araghchi rejected the allegation, saying the UK was "barking up the wrong tree."
* The five men, aged between 23 and 25, were arrested Sunday after police were alerted to three suspicious vehicles near the base. Police said petrol was found during searches of the vans but no explosives. All five were later released on bail.
* RAF Fairford has been used by U.S. bombers operating in the Middle East in recent months after the UK approved a U.S. request to use the base for strikes on Iran.
* **IRGC claims six militants killed in southeastern Iran:** Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e7ea4258-03b7-4806-bee1-56b6793bd9cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday its forces killed six people in an operation against a group it alleged was planning an attack in the southeastern province of Sistan and Baluchestan.
* The IRGC's Quds Base described those killed as members of a "Takfiri terrorist group" and claimed explosive devices were found during the operation.

# Yemen
* **Saudi-backed forces, Ansarallah report strikes in Taiz and Saada:**
* **Taiz, southwestern Yemen:** Saudi-backed forces carried out six airstrikes on Ansarallah positions in Al-Akboosh and on fronts in Haifan district, the government forces said.
* Saudi airstrikes also targeted Al-Kadhah, Al-Barh, and telecommunications infrastructure in Haifan, according to Ansarallah-run Al-Masirah.
* **Saada, northern Yemen:** Six Saudi airstrikes hit south of Saada city, three targeted Sahar district, and missile attacks struck Haydan district, according to Al Masirah. Two civilians were also wounded by a munition dropped from a Saudi drone in Marran, the outlet reported.
* **Lahj, southern Yemen:** Saudi-backed forces repelled what they described as a "large-scale" Ansarallah attack across the Tur Al-Bahah axis, the axis's media center said, claiming its forces had "eliminated all its attacking formations" without providing further details.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed and 26 injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,040 killed, with 175,168 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,439 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,052, while 834 bodies have been recovered.
* **Israeli attacks continue as 105 bodies recovered from Gaza City rubble are buried:** Several Palestinians were [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/f5860ff1-0684-4758-9e39-9ef00b028472?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday when an Israeli drone targeted Al-Mawasi in Khan Younis, WAFA reported.
* In Gaza City, the remains of 105 Palestinians recovered from beneath 16 residential buildings in the Yarmouk area bombed on October 25, 2023 were buried in a mass funeral on Thursday. The recovered bodies included 37 children and 38 women.
* More than 8,000 bodies remain beneath rubble across the Strip, according to Gaza's Civil Defense.

* **Israeli strike kills Palestinian journalist in Gaza, bringing journalist death toll to 263:** Palestinian journalist Mohammed Abdul Aziz al-Najjar was [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/fa68c081-9169-4753-a974-0a6cc613c1a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday in an Israeli strike on his hometown of Khuza'a, east of Khan Younis, according to Gaza's Government Media Office, which said his death brought the number of journalists killed by Israeli forces in Gaza to 263. Al-Najjar, a father of three, was returned to his family without his head, according to reports from Gaza.
* **Israeli settlers attack Palestinians, steal olive harvest across the occupied West Bank:**
* **Salfit:** Two Palestinians were [wounded](https://substack.com/redirect/6cddd023-7ea8-46ac-8c8a-a73678b4e68f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by live fire during a settler attack on homes in Yasuf, east of Salfit, on Thursday, according to WAFA. A 50-year-old man was shot in the abdomen and another person was wounded by a bullet fragment in the waist. Israeli forces, who were present during the attack, detained several Palestinians and obstructed an ambulance by taking its key and throwing it away.
* **Jenin:** Israeli settlers [stole](https://substack.com/redirect/fcbde7c7-71a7-4887-b167-471a7ffd4e6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olives from Palestinian-owned land in Kafr Ra'i, Faqqu'a, Deir Abu Da'if, Ya'bad and other areas near Israeli settlements, as the annual picking season gets underway, WAFA reported.
* **Nablus:** Settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/e5ae4e5a-4507-4859-813b-c5abb39243a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Palestinian farmers picking olives in Odala, south of Nablus, and prevented them from harvesting in the village's plains.
* **Ramallah and Al-Bireh:** Settlers [stole](https://substack.com/redirect/2cb94a2b-ceb9-4d59-b142-16298bc6800c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olives from Palestinian land in Al-Mughayyir under the protection of Israeli forces. Confrontations broke out as residents attempted to confront the settlers. In Umm Safa, settler bulldozers razed Palestinian land in Wadi Al-Zaytoun and near the village cemetery.

# Lebanon
* **Israeli attacks continue across south Lebanon despite U.S.-brokered agreement:**
* **Nabatieh:** Israeli warplanes [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/ced40483-6e42-4686-84bd-c140bcc2140d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the outskirts of Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah on Thursday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Overnight, Israeli warplanes also struck the outskirts of Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah, while Israeli artillery intermittently shelled the Ali Al-Taher heights.
* **Tyre (Sour):** Israeli forces [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/0075c9c7-a775-4c70-b97a-8107903dcbbe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) several homes in Al-Mansouri on Thursday. Israeli warplanes also struck Al-Mansouri.
