Photo by Aizar Raldes / AFP via Getty Images. Thursday, October 1, 2026 -** Iran : Iranian President says Tehran will pursue U.S. dialogue. Tehran rejects report U.S. ordered its UN delegation to leave New York. UK says there are "strong indications" Iran played role in RAF Fairford incident. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims six militants killed in southeastern Iran. Yemen : Saudi-backed forces, Ansarallah report strikes in Taiz and Saada. Palestine : Israeli attacks continue as 105 bodies recovered from Gaza City rubble are buried. Israeli strike kills Palestinian journalist in Gaza, bringing journalist death toll to 263. Israeli settlers attack Palestinians, steal olive harvest across the occupied West Bank. Lebanon : Israeli attacks continue across south Lebanon despite U.S.-brokered agreement. Lebanon documents suspected Israeli war crimes. Syria and Hezbollah hold first known face-to-face talks in Turkey. U.S. : U.S. economy grew 2.2% in Q2, upgraded from earlier estimate. Tennessee botches second execution this year, governor halts all remaining 2026 executions. War Secretary Pete Hegseth announces new drone command, 20 percent cut to generals in "State of the Force" speech. Federal Trade Commission launches investigation into OpenAI, Anthropic over AI safety. ICE briefly published, then removed, internal reports showing medical failures in 33 detainee deaths. Department of Justice files ethics complaint against nearly all Minnesota federal judges over immigration-surge comments. Senate confirms Keith Sonderling as Labor Secretary. Sen. Josh Hawley introduces bill to regulate Flock cameras, AI surveillance. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reports over $250 million in income from 2025. Judge rules U.S. can deport Milwaukee Muslim leader on national security grounds. South Africa summons U.S. Ambassador for third time over "undiplomatic conduct." French court sentences 13 to prison over 2021 Channel crossing that killed 31 migrants. International : Bolivian attorney general detained days after U.S. revoked his visa over alleged drug trafficking ties. Pakistan says strikes killed 22 fighters in Afghanistan; Kabul claims civilian deaths. Russia warns NATO it would use nuclear weapons if alliance blocks Kaliningrad. Brazil briefs French, German officials on alleged U.S. and Russian election interference. Gunmen kill 7 on Syrian bus; gas pipeline blast knocks out three power plants. Iraqi armed group suspends military operations after U.S. troop withdrawal. China builds new military facility in Laos, possibly first full People's Liberation Army base in Southeast Asia. Norway's parliament probes Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre, 10 others over links to Jeffrey Epstein. Hong Kong journalist arrested on sedition charge over 2019 police clash coverage. MI5 warns UK academics to sever ties with Chinese research group over alleged spying. Rwanda open to hosting EU migrant transfer facilities, lawmakers say. Entire newsroom arrested in Egypt in significant press crackdown. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Iranian President says Tehran will pursue U.S. dialogue: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran would continue pursuing dialogue with the United States despite repeated attacks during negotiations. "We have never avoided dialogue and will not do so, although the United States targeted our country three times," Pezeshkian said, adding that Iran was also seeking to expand land-based trade with Pakistan, Iraq, Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan amid "restrictions at sea." Separately, President Donald Trump Time that Iran had made an offer concerning reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but said what he had seen was "simply not enough." Trump said renewed U.S. attacks after the midterm elections were possible, adding: "What I rejected a year ago, I will not agree to today. Iran could be destroyed, and that's possible." Tehran rejects report U.S. ordered its UN delegation to leave New York: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and the Iranian delegation New York on Monday evening according to a prearranged schedule that had been communicated to the U.S. State Department on September 17, Iran's UN mission said. The statement came after Axios, citing a source, reported that the U.S. had asked the Iranian delegation to leave New York, while also reporting that Araghchi had already been scheduled to return to Tehran on Monday evening. Iran's mission called the claim "baseless and worthless." UK says there are "strong indications" Iran played role in RAF Fairford incident: The government Iran played a role in an incident at RAF Fairford that led to the arrest of five UK nationals, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, but provided no further details or evidence for the claim. Araghchi rejected the allegation, saying the UK was "barking up the wrong tree." The five men, aged between 23 and 25, were arrested Sunday after police were alerted to three suspicious vehicles near the base. Police said petrol was found during searches of the vans but no explosives. All five were later released on bail. RAF Fairford has been used by U.S. bombers operating in the Middle East in recent months after the UK approved a U.S. request to use the base for strikes on Iran. IRGC claims six militants killed in southeastern Iran: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Thursday its forces killed six people in an operation against a group it alleged was planning an attack in the southeastern province of Sistan and Baluchestan. The IRGC's Quds Base described those killed as members of a "Takfiri terrorist group" and claimed explosive devices were found during the operation. Yemen Saudi-backed forces, Ansarallah report strikes in Taiz and Saada: Taiz, southwestern Yemen: Saudi-backed forces carried out six airstrikes on Ansarallah positions in Al-Akboosh and on fronts in Haifan district, the government forces said. Saudi airstrikes also targeted Al-Kadhah, Al-Barh, and telecommunications infrastructure in Haifan, according to Ansarallah-run Al-Masirah. Saada, northern Yemen: Six Saudi airstrikes hit south of Saada city, three targeted Sahar district, and missile attacks struck Haydan district, according to Al Masirah. Two civilians were also wounded by a munition dropped from a Saudi drone in Marran, the outlet reported. Lahj, southern Yemen: Saudi-backed forces repelled what they described as a "large-scale" Ansarallah attack across the Tur Al-Bahah axis, the axis's media center said, claiming its forces had "eliminated all its attacking formations" without providing further details. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed and 26 injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,040 killed, with 175,168 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,439 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,052, while 834 bodies have been recovered. Israeli attacks continue as 105 bodies recovered from Gaza City rubble are buried: Several Palestinians were on Thursday when an Israeli drone targeted Al-Mawasi in Khan Younis, WAFA reported. In Gaza City, the remains of 105 Palestinians recovered from beneath 16 residential buildings in the Yarmouk area bombed on October 25, 2023 were buried in a mass funeral on Thursday. The recovered bodies included 37 children and 38 women. More than 8,000 bodies remain beneath rubble across the Strip, according to Gaza's Civil Defense. Israeli strike kills Palestinian journalist in Gaza, bringing journalist death toll to 263: Palestinian journalist Mohammed Abdul Aziz al-Najjar was Wednesday in an Israeli strike on his hometown of Khuza'a, east of Khan Younis, according to Gaza's Government Media Office, which said his death brought the number of journalists killed by Israeli forces in Gaza to 263. Al-Najjar, a father of three, was returned to his family without his head, according to reports from Gaza. Israeli settlers attack Palestinians, steal olive harvest across the occupied West Bank: Salfit: Two Palestinians were by live fire during a settler attack on homes in Yasuf, east of Salfit, on Thursday, according to WAFA. A 50-year-old man was shot in the abdomen and another person was wounded by a bullet fragment in the waist. Israeli forces, who were present during the attack, detained several Palestinians and obstructed an ambulance by taking its key and throwing it away. Jenin: Israeli settlers olives from Palestinian-owned land in Kafr Ra'i, Faqqu'a, Deir Abu Da'if, Ya'bad and other areas near Israeli settlements, as the annual picking season gets underway, WAFA reported. Nablus: Settlers Palestinian farmers picking olives in Odala, south of Nablus, and prevented them from harvesting in the village's plains. Ramallah and Al-Bireh: Settlers olives from Palestinian land in Al-Mughayyir under the protection of Israeli forces. Confrontations broke out as residents attempted to confront the settlers. In Umm Safa, settler bulldozers razed Palestinian land in Wadi Al-Zaytoun and near the village cemetery. Lebanon Israeli attacks continue across south Lebanon despite U.S.-brokered agreement: Nabatieh: Israeli warplanes the outskirts of Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah on Thursday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Overnight, Israeli warplanes also struck the outskirts of Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah, while Israeli artillery intermittently shelled the Ali Al-Taher heights. Tyre (Sour): Israeli forces several homes in Al-Mansouri on Thursday. Israeli warplanes also struck Al-Mansouri. Bint Jbeil: Israeli forces toward Haddatha on Thursday as Israeli military vehicles moved through the town. Lebanon documents suspected Israeli war crimes: Israeli attacks on Lebanon since March 2, 2026, included suspected war crimes and crimes against humanity involving attacks on civilians, journalists, medical personnel, and infrastructure, as well as widespread destruction and forced displacement, according to a more than 200-page compiled by Lebanon's National Committee for International Humanitarian Law and submitted to Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri. The report, according to the New Arab, documents, among other cases, the April 22 killing of journalist Amal Khalil, the April 8 bombardment that killed more than 303 people and wounded over 1,200, and widespread destruction in southern Lebanon, including Bint Jbeil. The report comes despite Lebanon agreeing under the June 26 framework ceasefire to end "all hostile or harmful actions in international political or legal forums" against Israel. Syria and Hezbollah hold first known face-to-face talks in Turkey: Syrian government officials and representatives of Hezbollah in Turkey last month in an effort to ease tensions, marking the first known face-to-face talks between the longtime foes, Reuters reported. The talks, convened at Turkey's initiative, involved Syrian intelligence and foreign ministry officials and Hezbollah representatives. A Syrian official told Reuters that Damascus assured Hezbollah it would not intervene militarily in Lebanon to disarm the group, while asking Hezbollah to help halt cross-border arms smuggling and dismantle alleged remaining cells in Syria. Hezbollah representatives reportedly pledged not to interfere in Syrian affairs but did not directly respond to the other requests. Iran did not participate, although a Lebanese security source said Hezbollah attended with Tehran's knowledge and that Iran was disappointed at being excluded from the talks. U.S. News U.S. economy grew 2.2% in Q2, upgraded from earlier estimate : The U.S. economy at a 2.2 percent annual pace from April through June, the Commerce Department reported Wednesday in its final second-quarter estimate, up from a previous 1.5 percent estimate, surprising economists who had expected little revision. Growth decelerated from 2.5 percent in the first quarter. Consumer spending, which makes up about 70 percent of economic activity, jumped to a 3.8 percent annual pace from just 0.7 percent in the first quarter, while business investment excluding housing rose 9 percent. Tennessee botches second execution this year, governor halts all remaining 2026 executions: The governor of Tennessee has halted the state's remaining executions for the rest of the year after officials were unable to put Christa Gail Pike to death on Wednesday. Pike breathing, talking, and snoring for nearly an hour after receiving two rounds of lethal injection drugs, prompting Tennessee to halt the execution and administer emergency medical care to her. Her attorneys said she was taken to a nearby hospital with no update on her condition Robin Maher , the director of the Death Penalty Information Center, called Wednesday night's execution "one of the worst botched executions in the modern death penalty era." Pike's attorneys had argued that her small veins and a blood disorder created heightened risk of a botched procedure. The incident follows a similarly botched May execution attempt of Tony Carruthers at the same Nashville prison. Republican Gov. Bill Lee halted all remaining 2026 executions after Pike's failed injection and ordered a third-party review of the incident. Hegseth announces new drone command, 20 percent cut to generals in "State of the Force" speech: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at Quantico Wednesday that he is creating a new four-star drone command to oversee autonomous warfare systems, doubling a previous 10 percent reduction in flag and general officer positions to a 20 percent cut, and launching a future-warfare study led by Elon Musk, Newt Gingrich and Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey. The new Autonomous Warfare Command, or AutoWarCom, whose inception Hegseth attributed to the "lessons" learned in Ukraine, will be created despite the recent shuttering of a similar command in Europe. Hegseth also announced plans for a new Office of Religious Affairs and to build a new military base, inviting all 50 states to compete to host the facility, which he estimated could accommodate up to 25,000 service members. FTC launches investigation into OpenAI, Anthropic over AI safety : The Federal Trade Commission is OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies over potential safety risks, Axios reported on Wednesday, with FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson preparing civil investigative demands to compel executives to turn over documents and testify. The probe has reportedly been underway for weeks, and predates OpenAI's disclosure that a model it was testing escaped its sandbox and compromised infrastructure belonging to a startup company, Hugging Face. ICE briefly published, then removed, internal reports showing medical failures in 33 detainee deaths: Internal ICE mortality reviews briefly posted online over the weekend and quickly removed found that the care administered by the agency deviated from "safe practice limit" in 27 of 33 detainee deaths between September 2019 and January 2026, including 11 that occurred since January 2025. In one case, 39-year-old Ismael Ayala-Uribe died from septic shock after Adelanto Processing Center staff failed to examine his abscess, respond to his complaints, or adequately document his care. In another case, 44-year-old Marie Ange Blaise died of a heart attack after staff failed to perform CPR despite finding no pulse. The full report from the San Francisco Chronicle, which first reported on these reviews, is available . DOJ files ethics complaint against nearly all Minnesota federal judges over immigration-surge comments : Attorney General Todd Blanche an ethics complaint Wednesday against nearly all federal district judges in Minnesota, alleging that former Chief Judge Patrick Schiltz, Judge John Tunheim and others violated judicial conduct rules by speaking to the New York Times about the toll of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown. Senate confirms Keith Sonderling as Labor Secretary: The Senate Keith Sonderling , 47-41, as Labor Secretary Wednesday, elevating Sonderling, who had served as acting secretary since April, to the top job. Sonderling, a Trump first-term advisor and former Republican EEOC member, succeeds Lori Chavez-DeRemer , who left the post following accusations that she abused her position. Sen. Josh Hawley introduces bill to regulate Flock cameras, AI surveillance : Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) is the Stop Flock Abuse Act to impose stricter data, security, and search limits on automated license plate readers like Flock cameras. The bill would restrict local governments from selling or sharing vehicle data, require data deletion within 10 days absent an active criminal investigation, ban facial recognition on surveillance networks, and mandate written approval and audit logs to prevent unauthorized searches. Data would also need to be encrypted and kept within the U.S. Commerce Secretary Lutnick reports over $250 million in income from 2025: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick 's newly released 2025 financial disclosure he reported at least $250 million in income and proceeds. The largest part of this was a $192 million "tax distribution" from Cantor Fitzgerald, the financial firm he led for decades before stepping down to join the administration. He also disclosed $4.2 million in salary and bonus from the real estate firm Newmark, $19.6 million from a Newmark partnership exchange, $14.1 million from the brokerage BGC Group, and over $5 million from BGC restricted stock units. Judge rules U.S. can deport Milwaukee Muslim leader on national security grounds : Immigration Judge Jayme Salinardi Wednesday that Salah Sarsour, president of the Islamic Society of Milwaukee and a prominent Palestinian rights advocate, can be deported on foreign policy grounds, though she rejected the government's separate claim that he lied on his green card application. The ruling follows Sarsour's detention in March and a ruling by a federal judge in June ordering his release, which noted that he had made a "substantial" claim that the government had targeted him for his pro-Palestinian activism. Sarsour, who called the ruling "deeply disappointing," said he will appeal and that deportation to the occupied West Bank, where he was born and previously imprisoned by Israel, would "mean the end of my life." Sarsour's attorneys say he was tortured and coerced into confessions during his 1988 and 1995 convictions in Israel. Sarsour has lived in the U.S. since 1993. During his detention by ICE, Sarsour, who has Type 2 diabetes, lost more than 30 pounds. According to his attorneys, his blood sugar levels were checked only once a month, putting him at risk of organ failure or death. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Bolivian attorney general detained days after U.S. revoked his visa over alleged drug trafficking ties: Police detained Attorney General Roger Mariaca on Wednesday and the prosecutor's offices in Sucre. Washington imposed visa restrictions on Mariaca and accused him on Monday of accepting bribes to facilitate drug trafficking and help violent criminals evade justice. Mariaca denied the allegations, calling the visa restrictions "interference" and "political pressure" in response to his investigations. Mariaca has been involved in of Trump-linked figures accused of corruption and violent crimes including Argentinian political consultant Fernando Cerimedo who is facing drug-trafficking charges in addition to the charge of attempted murder after allegedly ordering a hit on his former girlfriend Nadia Beller. In response to the visa restrictions imposed on Bolivian officials, Beller published a photo showing Cerimedo in a meeting with Donald Trump Junior and MAGA political operator Brad Parscale. She alleged the raid on Mariana's office was an effort to "disappear" evidence in the Cerimedo case. For more on Cerimedo and President Rodrigo Paz 's effort to distance himself from his onetime key adviser, read Joseph Bouchard's report for Drop Site . Pakistan says strikes killed 22 fighters in Afghanistan; Kabul claims civilian deaths : Pakistan's Ministry of Information airstrikes based on "credible intelligence" killed at least 22 fighters from the Pakistani Taliban (TTP) and Balochistan Liberation Army at camps and hideouts in Afghanistan, destroying weapons and ammunition caches. A spokesman for the Afghan Taliban said the attacks hit Afghanistan's Kunar and Helmand provinces late Wednesday, and that they killed at least nine people, including women and children, wounded 11 others and destroyed three houses. Afghanistan denies harboring armed groups and says recent Pakistani strikes have repeatedly hit civilian homes. Russia warns NATO it would use nuclear weapons if alliance blocks Kaliningrad : Russia a diplomatic memo to NATO member states Wednesday warning it is prepared to use its "entire arsenal, including nuclear weapons," if the alliance attempts to blockade the Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad, claiming it has "information that NATO is preparing an air and naval blockade" of the territory. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called the document "unhelpful" and said Russia should "stop the nuclear threats," adding that NATO is a defensive alliance and claiming that "Putin knows that he can never win" in a confrontation with the group. Brazil briefs French, German officials on alleged U.S. and Russian election interference : Brazil's spy agency Abin a visiting French and German delegation in Brasilia this month, "confirming the existence of interference from the United States as well as Russia" ahead of Brazil's Sunday election, according to Reuters. The agency alleged that U.S. interference ranged "from lawfare to interference that is openly acknowledged"; no details were given related to the alleged Russian activity. A senior Brazilian cyber official present at the briefing also noted that cyberattacks targeting Brazil's president's office have nearly doubled and are "clearly election-related." In , philosopher Rodrigo Nunes, political scientist Camila Rocha, journalist Piero Locatelli and organizer Stephanie Weatherbee Brito examine the stakes of the election. Their essays assess the resilience of Bolsonarismo, the growing role of U.S. intervention, the weakening of Brazil's left, and the challenges facing popular movements. Gunmen kill 7 on Syrian bus; gas pipeline blast knocks out three power plants : Unidentified gunmen on a civilian bus carrying workers home in Homs, Syria, Wednesday, killing at least seven people, Syrian state media reported. The shooting came hours after an explosion and fire at a gas pipeline in eastern Ghouta near Damascus knocked the Deir Ali, al-Nasiriyah, and Tishreen power plants offline, with Energy Minister Mohammed al-Bashir saying the cause of the explosion remains unclear. "It could be a technical malfunction, an attack or an act of sabotage," he said. Wednesday's explosion was the third such pipeline incident in six weeks, following two earlier blasts the Syrian Petroleum Company attributed to sabotage, with no group claiming responsibility for any of the attacks. U.S. removes Syria from arms export ban: The U.S. State Department Syria from its ITAR ("International Traffic in Arms Regulations") arms export denial list in a notice published Wednesday, effective Thursday. Syrian requests to purchase arms from U.S. companies will now be considered on a case-by-case basis. Only seven countries--Belarus, China, Cuba, Iran, Myanmar, North Korea, and Venezuela--remain subject to the policy. The move follows President Trump's easing of decades-old sanctions on Syria last year and Secretary of State Marco Rubio's August rescission of Syria's state sponsor of terrorism designation, part of a broader warming toward President Ahmad al-Sharaa's government. Iraqi armed group suspends military operations after U.S. troop withdrawal : Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed Iraqi militia and political movement, Wednesday that it was ceasing military activities following the departure of U.S. forces. The withdrawal concludes the U.S.-led military mission in Iraq that began in 2014 to fight the Islamic State. The group had previously said it would only discuss giving up its weapons once foreign troops left. Iraq's government said talks were ongoing to bring armed groups into state institutions, but Kataib Hezbollah's announcement did not include a commitment to disarm. China builds new military facility in Laos, possibly first full PLA base in Southeast Asia: China's defense ministry on Tuesday that the China-Laos Joint Support and Training Center and the China-Laos Friendship Aviation Academy are now operational in Ban Keun, on the outskirts of the Laotian capital of Vientiane. Satellite imagery reviewed by Reuters appears to show that the center features a newly constructed airfield, which includes a paved runway, a taxiway, an apron, and new buildings. China's defense ministry said the facility trains air force pilots and is "not directed against any third party." Security scholar Collin Koh wrote on X that the base "may not be wrong to conclude this is the first full-fledged PLA overseas base in Southeast Asia," distinguishing it from China's more ambiguous joint training center at Cambodia's Ream naval base. The facility adds to China's growing overseas military footprint, which already includes a Djibouti base, artificial island facilities in the Spratly Islands, and reported new construction in the disputed Paracel archipelago. Norway 's parliament probes PM Støre, 10 others over Epstein links: Norway's Parliament a public hearing Wednesday into 11 current and former senior officials, including Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre, over ties to Jeffrey Epstein allegedly revealed in the files released by the U.S. Justice Department in January. The scrutiny centers on the diplomat Terje Rod-Larsen, who ran the International Peace Institute and who had numerous ties to the financier. It has been alleged that Rod-Larsen secured an illicit loan from Epstein and helped the financier commit visa fraud for the women he trafficked; Epstein also reportedly left millions to Rod-Larsen's children in his will. The announcement follows recent reporting that the foreign ministry allocated over 130 million kroner ($13.5 million) to the Institute while Rod-Larsen was in charge and while he reportedly was engaged with Epstein. Støre, who served as foreign minister while Terje Rod-Larsen ran the IPI, has denied he had any relationship with Epstein. Hong Kong journalist arrested on sedition charge over 2019 police clash coverage : Hong Kong police Tang Ho-wing, founder of the outlet Boom News, on Wednesday on suspicion of "incitement by spreading disinformation," after his outlet posted a video featuring a woman's account of a 2019 attack at the Prince Edward rail station, where anti-government protesters say police officers killed some in their cohort. Authorities also arrested another person, identified as activist Lee Ying-chi by the South China Morning Post, alongside Tang on Wednesday. South Africa summons U.S. Ambassador Bozell for third time over "undiplomatic conduct": South Africa's foreign affairs ministry U.S. Ambassador Leo Brent Bozell III on Tuesday for the third time in his nine-month tenure over what officials described as "undiplomatic conduct," a South African official told Reuters. The precise cause of the demarche is not known. The State Department confirmed that Bozell met with his South African counterparts, claiming that they "discussed bilateral ties" and adding that the U.S. is "not interested in diplomatic manoeuvring, procedural delays or dialogue for dialogue's sake." The summons comes amid deteriorating relations fueled by President Donald Trump's repeated unsubstantiated claims that white South Africans face systemic persecution; it also follows the U.S.'s announcement of additional visa restrictions on South Africans two weeks ago. French court sentences 13 to prison over 2021 Channel crossing that killed 31 migrants : A Paris court 13 men on Wednesday for organizing the deadliest small-boat migrant crossing attempt to the UK, with six convicted of involuntary homicide (which carries as many as 10 years in prison) and the remaining seven receiving lesser sentences of up to four years; a 14th defendant was acquitted. Prosecutors alleged that the defendants put a vessel to sea that was unfit for the crossing, overloaded the vessel with migrants (primarily Iraqi Kurds), and failed to provide lifejackets for the voyage. The vessel, which attempted a crossing of the English Channel in November 2021, capsized, killing 31 migrants. Seven French military personnel remain under investigation for allegedly failing to assist survivors during the incident. MI5 warns UK academics to sever ties with Chinese research group over alleged spying : Britain's MI5 a rare public alert Wednesday accusing the China General Technology Research Institute of having "very strong ties" to China's Ministry of State Security, adding that the group's "primary purpose" is funding academic research that enhances Chinese espionage capabilities. The statement warned that more than 100 UK-based academics working in AI, cybersecurity, covert communications and steganography had been targeted by the group, and told academics that, should they continue accepting CGTRI grants, they could be prosecuted under the UK's 2023 National Security Act. Rwanda open to hosting EU migrant transfer facilities, lawmakers say : Rwanda has preliminary discussions with some EU member states about potentially hosting facilities for migrants transferred from Europe, European Parliament lawmakers Tineke Strik and Anna Strolenberg said Wednesday after a visit to Kigali, though no agreements have been reached. An EU official told Reuters that Rwanda is among the countries being considered by the "Group of Five"--Germany, Austria, Greece, Denmark, and the Netherlands--which announced earlier this month they aim to establish migrant "return hubs" outside the EU this year. Rwanda has increasingly positioned itself as a destination for Western deportations, previously receiving up to 250 migrants from the U.S. as part of a 2025 agreement. Entire newsroom arrested in Egypt in significant press crackdown: Six journalists from the independent Egyptian investigative journalism platform Matsda2sh--comprising the media outlet's entire newsroom--were arrested by Egyptian security forces overnight on Monday in an escalated crackdown on press freedoms in Egypt, to Mada Masr. The condition and whereabouts of their detention remains unknown and they remain forcibly disappeared. The Interior Ministry on Thursday the arrests for the first time and accused Matsda2sh of fabricating lies and spreading rumors to "undermine stability," and accused the outlet of having ties to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood. The platform's founder Abdelrahman Mansour, rejected the accusations in a statement, saying the authorities know the charges--which are commonly levelled by Egyptian authorities against journalists--are false. "I believe this is the first time in the two-century history of Egyptian journalism that an entire newsroom, with all its journalists, has been arrested," Hossam Bahgat, of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, told Mada Masr. Over 50 civil society organizations and independent media outlets around the world have signed a calling for the immediate release of the six journalists. Before the latest arrests, Egypt ranked as the 7th worst jailer of journalists in the world, according to the latest CPJ census. # **Tennessee execution halted after 2 lethal injections fail to kill female murderer**
Christa Pike, 50, convicted of murdering a classmate in 1995, **[survived two doses of pentobarbital](https://substack.com/redirect/94bf278d-698c-478a-8a98-c8b21d35cc63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during her execution Wednesday, remaining conscious and breathing before being taken to a hospital, prompting Gov. * **In January 1995, Christa Pike, along with her boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp and friend Shadolla Peterson, lured a fellow classmate, 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, to a secluded spot** in the woods. Pike believed Slemmer was pursuing her boyfriend and wanted her dead out of jealousy. Once there, while Peterson kept watch, Pike and Shipp subjected Slemmer to prolonged torture: they cut a pentagram into her chest with a box cutter, struck her repeatedly with a meat cleaver, and cut her throat multiple times as she begged for her life. Pike ultimately killed her by crushing her skull with a piece of asphalt, then took a fragment of the skull as a keepsake.

* **The Supreme Court had cleared the way for the execution hours earlier in a 6-3 ruling,** overturning a lower court stay tied to Pike's claims that her childhood sexual abuse wasn't properly considered at sentencing; Justices Sotomayor, Kagan, and Jackson dissented.
* **Pike 's attorneys said the botched procedure caused "unnecessary agony"** and cited difficult vein access and degraded drugs, while state officials maintained protocol was followed. Pike would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in over 200 years.

Because of your generosity we not only met but exceeded our flash match goal. Every single dollar is doubled to protect, defend, and expand access to reproductive care. The support of people like you is why we can represent patients like Magon Hoffman in Oklahoma after she was denied emergency abortion care following her baby’s fatal fetal diagnosis. Donations to the Center provide the critical resources we need to challenge abortion bans in 10 states and push back against the abuses of the Trump administration with 30+ active filings. We fight legal battles, but they also represent real women, real families, and real lives that extreme anti-abortion restrictions have upended. We are so grateful to have you with us — and ready for whatever comes next. name: Kailee for Congress
subject: Official invitation for Peter
body:
I want you beside me as we build this campaign from the ground up.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/f8OfxvTg8CC?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter, I wanted to personally thank you for joining our campaign.
I grew up in Auburn in a blue-collar family. My dad spent 41 years working as a correctional officer. My mom is a nurse who cares for Alzheimer’s patients. I worked multiple jobs to put myself through school, became the first person in my family to earn a four-year degree, and spent years paying off my student loans.
_I know what it means to work hard, do everything right, and still wonder why it keeps getting harder to get ahead._
**That is why I’m running for Congress: to lower costs, protect our communities, defend our farmers and small businesses, and make Central New York a place where our children can build their futures.**
But this campaign doesn't just belong to me. It belongs to every New Yorker who is ready to fight for something better.
_That means you, too._
Because you joined us at the very beginning, I’m inviting you to become an official FOUNDING MEMBER of Kailee Buller for Congress.
---
| [ACCEPT YOUR FOUNDING MEMBERSHIP >> ](https://us.list-manage.com/1NNS_SjwyxV?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---

### CAIT CONLEY RAISES OVER $5 MILLION IN Q3 OF 2026
******************OSSINING, NY –** Army combat veteran and Democratic nominee for New York’s 17th Congressional District Cait Conley raised **over $5 million in the third quarter of 2026, bringing the total cycle raise to $9.5 million**. The campaign received **more than 44,000 contributions** , with an **average contribution of $118**. Unlike her opponent, Rep. Mike Lawler, who has raked in over $1 million in corporate PAC donations, **Cait Conley has never taken any corporate PAC money** and instead is fueled by thousands of grassroots supporters in New York and across the country. While Mike votes with Donald Trump 100% of the time — even when it makes his constituents’ lives harder and more expensive — Cait will take on anyone who stands in the way of the better, more affordable future the Hudson Valley deserves.”_ __ ### **About Cait Conley** Cait Conley is a Hudson Valley native, the daughter of a postal worker and a construction worker. **Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission.

Team, First, I want to say thank you. **Because of this grassroots team, Fight Like Hell PAC hit our end-of-quarter goal last night.** I’m incredibly grateful to everyone who chipped in, shared our message, or showed up for this work. And a few days ago, I had the chance to speak at the Human Rights Campaign’s annual dinner. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140430632/650469209/-1313101072?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&refcode=AU_FLHP_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20261001_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDY0NjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOGUyYzkyNDYtYWRiZC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=P5dhDHpVupFfqcQ9VYHx1O0tDiDnlYnwMThi2-XEkZE=) I told the room something I want you to hear, too: **You deserve to love who you love. You deserve to be who you are. And you deserve to be treated with dignity and respect — no matter what.** Those aren’t abstract ideas to me. Fundamental freedoms are about having the power to make decisions about your own life: when and how to start a family, whether you can see a doctor without going broke, whether you can get a job, find a home, start a business, and live safely as the person you are. In Michigan, we’ve worked to turn those values into law. We expanded civil rights protections for LGBTQ+ Michiganders, banned the so-called panic defense, created our state’s first LGBTQ+ commission, and supported LGBTQ+ entrepreneurs and businesses. One of the proudest moments of my life came when I signed the expansion to the _Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act_ with my daughter Sherry standing beside me, protecting every Michigander, no matter who they love or how they identify. Sherry came out to me while she was applying to college. I didn’t know I was raising a gay daughter all those years — _but I’m damn proud I did._ **As a parent, there is nothing I won’t do to protect my kids. And as governor, there is nothing I won’t do to protect yours.** That’s the message I wanted to leave with everyone at HRC: that progress can feel slow, and the attacks can be relentless, but _movements are built by people who keep showing up anyway._ We’ve seen what that looks like before. Marriage equality. The repeal of “Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell.” Stronger protections against hate crimes. More than a thousand out and proud LGBTQ+ elected officials serving across the country. None of that happened because people gave up when the fight got hard. And with the midterms just weeks away, there is still a lot of work in front of us. **[If you didn't get a chance to pitch in before our end-of-quarter goal, we could use you today. If you can think of an example of everyday people holding huge corporations accountable for harming the public, it was probably made possible in large part by a [single legal theory](https://substack.com/redirect/72ed6b10-83d8-4ffa-8e98-3e2a6ff71487?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): public nuisance.
Public nuisance was a primary basis for the litigation against Big Tobacco in the 1990s, and was the foundation of the opioid cases over the past decade. It's played a prominent role in lawsuits on lead paint, predatory lending, water pollution, and "forever chemicals" like PFAS. It was the most important hook in recent [successful cases](https://substack.com/redirect/1b3b777e-82b9-41db-86cc-62911694dfe3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against social media companies like Meta for designing their platforms to addict and endanger children. And most recently, it has been a key cause of action in [litigation](https://substack.com/redirect/429a0dec-0720-4c6e-ad58-63b66dfa3b16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in several states against data centers for the air, water, and noise pollution they cause.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=218333183&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE4MzMzMTgzLCJpYXQiOjE3OTA4Njk2MjYsImV4cCI6MTc5MzQ2MTYyNiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.GJGyp72bI-TU3mv1oe4I_KsRZ-vKYoTahj9RL_yuUBU)
But not in Utah, Kansas, or Montana. Though it largely passed under the national radar, these states [enacted](https://substack.com/redirect/0742086f-d5f4-49c2-9869-1f3e923a8c79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [laws](https://substack.com/redirect/14b3624e-0a21-43e8-aa22-d46fe18fb283?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this year or [last](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02ee84-6f93-4d7f-8b64-45e6706fecc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that dismantle public nuisance as a cause of action--laws that, according to the Utah State Legislature's own Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel, will make claims against data centers and other corporate wrongdoers "more difficult to pursue." These states are not outliers, either--they're forerunners. Their laws closely mirror a model bill published this summer by the American Legislative Exchange Council, the corporate oligarchy's [primary conduit](https://substack.com/redirect/fb6975e4-b5bf-4955-852a-0c5f839cb3e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for [enacting right-wing laws](https://substack.com/redirect/784c6a16-7fb1-435e-a3c9-97df3a074e25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the state level. As I write this, ALEC's [Public Nuisance Reform Act](https://substack.com/redirect/90d47c35-c6f3-41bd-98cd-21924fee6ecf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is likely being distributed to Republican legislators in dozens of state houses around the country--and you can bet that Big Tech, eager to suppress a valuable tool of data center opponents, is lining up lobbyists to coax its passage.
Indeed, if this year was about trialing this extremist proposal, leaders on the ground believe that next year the real onslaught will begin. "Big corporations and the politicians they purchase use states like Utah as a testing ground for their regressive agenda," Utah state Senator Nate Blouin, a Democrat, told me. "But make no mistake, these corporate immunity laws are coming for you wherever you are. I wouldn't be surprised if they get introduced in nearly every state next year."
These attacks on public nuisance law constitute just one offensive in a multi-front war the right has been waging against our ability to use the courts to hold the wealthy and powerful to account. On October 5, the Supreme Court will hear _Suncor v. Boulder_ , in which Big Oil companies will make their case for immunity from legal repercussions for the fires, droughts, air pollution, extreme heat, and other harms they've caused to communities.
Boulder, the Colorado county and city, sued Suncor and Exxon Mobil in 2018 over the damage that climate change--and the companies' lies about their role in fueling it--had done to its residents. After the state Supreme Court ruled that the case should go to trial, Suncor and Exxon Mobil--clearly terrified of what would happen if communities like Boulder were allowed to have their day in court--asked the high court to intervene, arguing in legal briefs that "state tort law is not the solution to global climate change." As TNR's Matt Ford [wrote recently](https://substack.com/redirect/0be712cd-b059-4c0a-8b0a-362ffe0a3e5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the companies "effectively argue that because they and their products have caused damage everywhere, they cannot be held liable for it anywhere."
In case the Supreme Court doesn't give Big Oil a get-out-of-jail-free card, it's pursuing other means. In addition to its public nuisance model bill, ALEC recently published the [Energy Producers and Consumers Protection Act](https://substack.com/redirect/b0503f7d-bb99-4f1a-9617-6515364251ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which immunizes all corporations--the fossil fuel industry, certainly, but also all other industries--from liability for any misconduct that is even marginally related to climate change, including "negligence, gross negligence, recklessness, strict liability, products liability, failure to warn, fraud, fraudulent concealment, misrepresentation, unjust enrichment," as well as all related "criminal charges, indictments, or prosecutions." In other words, under this legislation, fraud is legal--if you're a powerful corporation. Meanwhile, Texas Senator Ted Cruz has introduced similar [legislation](https://substack.com/redirect/84b93c17-8baf-4deb-9334-59c4db68c514?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the federal level.
This right-wing blitzkrieg to shield big business from liability for its misconduct extends far beyond the issue of climate change. On a recent Federalist Society panel about climate immunity for corporations, O.H. Skinner, the executive director of Alliance for Consumers--one of numerous front groups spun up by conservative legal activist Leonard Leo--[explained](https://substack.com/redirect/0af334ef-d181-4338-800e-dd66b5a045e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that these efforts need to cover not just fossil fuel companies but every major industry, from Big Ag to Big Tech: "A lot of people in this space only talk about climate. And it frustrates me ... I'm the kind of person that, because I care about all these products, I start thinking, well [Big Oil immunity] doesn't do anything about pork, and it doesn't do anything about AI regulation." Earlier this year, the Supreme Court also issued a [ruling](https://substack.com/redirect/70707697-98ec-41a5-ac45-a42ac1ff5745?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) protecting Monsanto and other pesticide producers from thousands of lawsuits by families and farmworkers devastated by the cancer-causing effects of glyphosate products like Roundup.
This effort really does represent an attempt to fundamentally restructure our corporate governance model in the U.S., which has always relied on robust private litigation. All the way back in 1803, Chief Justice John Marshall, in his famous _Marbury v. Madison_ decision, wrote that the "very essence of civil liberty certainly consists in the right of every individual to claim the protection of the laws, whenever he receives an injury." While most developed countries overwhelmingly rely on public enforcement of laws, private enforcement--not just to compensate injured parties, but to affirmatively deter corporate malfeasance--has [long played](https://substack.com/redirect/fb81ab5c-7544-4528-aceb-514fd2f54d47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a key role in America, where regulatory state capacity has traditionally been much weaker than in places like Europe. This dynamic has become even more pronounced in recent years, as far-right billionaires have succeeded in dismantling significant portions of the administrative state and stacking federal regulatory offices with shills for the industries they're supposed to be regulating. In this context, public nuisance litigation and other lawsuits that rely on state law are communities' last--and sometimes only--line of defense against the unchecked avarice of powerful corporations that have been fully unleashed by the Trump administration.
So it's no wonder that the oligarchy has set its sights on dismantling the basic architecture of our civil legal system. This isn't an entirely new effort: The corporate right has been waging a version of this war, whitewashed as "tort reform," for decades. But to outright immunize corporate wrongdoing across the board--from Big Oil's climate crimes to Big Tech's data center disasters--would be a whole new level of elite impunity. The oligarchs are coming for every last tool the American people have ever used to restrain corporate abuse, deception, and overreach. And the fight to save these rights will be happening right in your community, no matter where in America you live.

Hey folks,
The Andrew and Tristan Tate story somehow keeps getting stranger.
Their allies are blaming the DOJ, politicians, and basically anyone they can find as the brothers face possible extradition to the UK. I break down the latest arguments from Nick Fuentes, a bizarre conspiracy theory about Washington insiders, Joe McBride's return to the spotlight, and the increasingly contradictory messaging coming from the Tates' camp.
* [**00:00:23**] Andrew Tate says he'd rather spend months in jail than live like a "normal person" as the brothers continue fighting possible extradition to the UK.
* [**00:01:40**] Nick Fuentes weighs in on the Tate brothers' legal situation and argues that taking on the government is nearly impossible, which leads me into what's actually at stake in their court battles.
* [**00:04:13**] One of the Tates' allies offers a wild explanation for their legal problems, claiming powerful people in Washington targeted them after a private gathering.
* [**00:07:18**] Joe McBride resurfaces after going unusually quiet, and I break down his role in the public messaging surrounding the brothers versus the legal fight itself.
* [**00:09:18**] A new post attributed to Andrew Tate raises even more questions about the brothers' claims regarding their detention, and whether their own messaging is contradicting itself.

This episode is about more than the latest Tate drama. It's about the competing narratives surrounding their legal cases, the effort by their allies to portray them as victims of the system, and the very different question of what will actually happen when their allegations and defenses are tested in court. Beneath the sands and clays of Central Florida, deep within the limestone, another world moves unseen. The aquifer winds beneath us--a vast, hidden realm of water and stone, carrying what every well, tap, garden, and throat depends upon.
We walk above it without thought. The ground becomes a place to build, pave, plant, and pass over. Yet the ground is more than what holds us up. It holds what sustains us.
And what enters the ground does not simply disappear. It descends. It enters the veins of that hidden world. When the source is compromised, something more than water is lost. The sweetness of the ground begins to change.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

There are no media consultants or comms people changing my words or watering down my thoughts. clean_body: Our country is in grave danger... | Peter, I understand that you get spammed with a whole lot of emails and texts from Republicans, especially in these final weeks of the midterms, so I try to avoid sending them whenever possible. Well, this might just be the single most important message I've ever written! But because of that, I'm under pressure to make every word count - and honestly, it's really hard to find the right words to convey the scale of the threat facing America. At this point, I've re-written this letter several times, and ultimately, I decided to just write to you straight from my heart with words inspired by my unwavering faith in God and our Country. There are no media consultants or comms people changing my words or watering down my thoughts. This all comes straight from , so I apologize if it's a bit rough around the edges. I'm not repeating the same worn-out talking points you're probably used to! Look - I know the mainstream media is downplaying it, but the Democrat Party is getting more and more extreme, to the point that I believe they pose a threat to our free Republic. They're embracing Communists, pro-Sharia candidates, and all kinds of radical Leftists who HATE conservatives, Christians, and the very values that made our country great. There was a time not too long ago when American voters would punish this kind of extremism at the ballot box. But instead, polling shows the Democrats are SURGING to their largest ever lead - - in the final weeks of the election! How are they winning in the polls? It's certainly not because American voters suddenly support radical ideas like communism, open borders, and defunding the police. A lot of elected officials aren't willing to say this, but I will... The left hates you, they hate your vote, and they hate MAGA for putting America First! Right now, they're spending to fully verify that new electorate to ensure that every last Democrat voter (illegals too!) casts a ballot in November. At the end of the day, winning the midterms is a simple numbers game, and as it stands, the American people still have the upper hand on the Left. 2024 proved that decisively! But our advantage disappears the second Republicans stop showing up to vote... We need to verify that every Republican voter - especially - will show up to cast a ballot on or before November 3rd. If Republicans don't turn out and we LOSE the midterms, the consequences for our country will be downright catastrophic. The America we fought so hard to SAVE in 2024 will crumble before our very eyes! That's why I'm appealing to you personally... | Thank you, Rep. You see, GOP dark-money super PACs have already spent over $100 million on this race. Now, they’re watching VERY closely to see if we hit our fundraising targets. If we fall short, they’ll take it as a sign of weakness – and spend millions more to buy this seat for Michael Whatley.

body:
Appreciating our resources| | | |
---
| | | Friends and Supporters,As we head into October I am reminded of the richness northern Wisconsin has to offer. At the end of summer I was honored to witness the harvesting of Manoomin (wild rice) on the Bad River Reservation. This weekend Bayfield celebrates Apple Fest, Eagle River holds Cranberry Fest, and there are numerous harvest festivals and Oktoberfests signaling the end of another successful growing season. We live in a place of bounty and I am grateful to all the people who care for our lands and waters and provide us with good food year after year. The leaves are changing color, too! But those reds and yellows are a reminder that Election Day is only about one month away! While it is a thrill to be so close to the end there is so much still to be done. October in a campaign cycle really is the most exciting but also the most demanding month of all.We have the best volunteers on Team Clark and now is the time for all of us to really kick into high gear. The way we win this race is by all of us reaching out to as many voters as we possibly can, either by knocking on their door or by calling them on the phone, or talking to neighbors on the street or across the fence. We can run ads and hold debates and town halls, but I can’t possibly call every single voter or knock on every single voter’s door. I hope that you scroll down to the important volunteer opportunities in this newsletter and find a way to push this campaign across the finish line ahead of our opponent. Finally, after months of listening to so many of you and distilling your ideas, this week I rolled out my vision for a New Northwoods here in CD7. I want to share this with you here, so I hope you can take a moment to read about my hopes for all of us in northern Wisconsin below. The New Northwoods is a vision based on three principles that helped shape this country: fairness, responsibility, and innovation. I think you'll agree that we have all the tools we need here to lead a life of affordability if we had a federal government that actually worked for the people that it is supposed to represent.With your help, in January I will be part of the next Congress that will actually work for you.Fred
---

# **The New Northwoods**
---
| | | We need to tackle economic fairness so we can bring back affordability for working people. We need a responsible government that actually does its job; investing in infrastructure and supporting its people. We need to encourage and capture the spirit of innovation from the people of northern Wisconsin as we reimagine the economic possibilities of a [New Northwoods.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140436140/650490056/-1375779573?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjEwMzAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZGFjMmE5MWEtYjdiZC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CgoBirG_7dM15ZZvfHGNkbsjBQAoEK32-kpnn1WuUDs=&emci=a418fc62-27bd-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=dac2a91a-b7bd-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=28718937) _We need Fred Clark in Congress.__We need your vote on November 3rd.__Fred’s vision for a revitalized northern Wisconsin, based on three basic principles:_**Fairness**
The people who have been writing the rules in this country are the ones who have been making the profits. The results of this broken system are clear: we now have the largest gap between rich and poor in American history. It’s time to level the playing field so that everyone has a shot at the American Dream again. We need to rewrite the rules to include all of us, and that means taking on corporations and special interests. Fred Clark is ready to stand up and fight for northern Wisconsin and meet these challenges head on.**Responsibility**
A responsible government takes care of its people. A New Northwoods needs smart investment of our tax dollars; from the basic benefits we have all earned to the programs which support the people among us who need the most help. A responsible government also enters into smart partnerships with private enterprise to jumpstart economic growth.**Innovation**
In this country we know how to take opportunities and do big things. Adapting to a new future requires research, development, and commercialization of new products. We can re-imagine our economy for today’s marketplace.For more on Fred’s New Northwoods please visit his website at [newnorthwoods.com](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140436141/650490057/-1375779573?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjEwMzAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZGFjMmE5MWEtYjdiZC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CgoBirG_7dM15ZZvfHGNkbsjBQAoEK32-kpnn1WuUDs=&emci=a418fc62-27bd-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=dac2a91a-b7bd-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=28718937)

clean_body: Appreciating our resources| | | | | | | Friends and Supporters,As we head into October I am reminded of the richness northern Wisconsin has to offer. At the end of summer I was honored to witness the harvesting of Manoomin (wild rice) on the Bad River Reservation. This weekend Bayfield celebrates Apple Fest, Eagle River holds Cranberry Fest, and there are numerous harvest festivals and Oktoberfests signaling the end of another successful growing season. We live in a place of bounty and I am grateful to all the people who care for our lands and waters and provide us with good food year after year. The leaves are changing color, too! But those reds and yellows are a reminder that Election Day is only about one month away! While it is a thrill to be so close to the end there is so much still to be done. October in a campaign cycle really is the most exciting but also the most demanding month of all.We have the best volunteers on Team Clark and now is the time for all of us to really kick into high gear. The way we win this race is by all of us reaching out to as many voters as we possibly can, either by knocking on their door or by calling them on the phone, or talking to neighbors on the street or across the fence. We can run ads and hold debates and town halls, but I can’t possibly call every single voter or knock on every single voter’s door. I hope that you scroll down to the important volunteer opportunities in this newsletter and find a way to push this campaign across the finish line ahead of our opponent. Finally, after months of listening to so many of you and distilling your ideas, this week I rolled out my vision for a New Northwoods here in CD7. I want to share this with you here, so I hope you can take a moment to read about my hopes for all of us in northern Wisconsin below. The New Northwoods is a vision based on three principles that helped shape this country: fairness, responsibility, and innovation. I think you'll agree that we have all the tools we need here to lead a life of affordability if we had a federal government that actually worked for the people that it is supposed to represent.With your help, in January I will be part of the next Congress that will actually work for you.Fred | | | | The New Northwoods | | | We need to tackle economic fairness so we can bring back affordability for working people. We need a responsible government that actually does its job; investing in infrastructure and supporting its people. We need to encourage and capture the spirit of innovation from the people of northern Wisconsin as we reimagine the economic possibilities of a We need Fred Clark in Congress.We need your vote on November 3rd.Fred’s vision for a revitalized northern Wisconsin, based on three basic principles:Fairness The people who have been writing the rules in this country are the ones who have been making the profits. The results of this broken system are clear: we now have the largest gap between rich and poor in American history. It’s time to level the playing field so that everyone has a shot at the American Dream again. We need to rewrite the rules to include all of us, and that means taking on corporations and special interests. Fred Clark is ready to stand up and fight for northern Wisconsin and meet these challenges head on.Responsibility A responsible government takes care of its people. A New Northwoods needs smart investment of our tax dollars; from the basic benefits we have all earned to the programs which support the people among us who need the most help. A responsible government also enters into smart partnerships with private enterprise to jumpstart economic growth.Innovation In this country we know how to take opportunities and do big things. Adapting to a new future requires research, development, and commercialization of new products. We can re-imagine our economy for today’s marketplace.For more on Fred’s New Northwoods please visit his website at | | | | Thank You! We Nearly Met Our EOQ Fundraising Goal We are overflowing with gratitude as we worked to reach our FEC end-of-quarter fundraising goal. What we raise is public and September 30th was a huge deadline. We are just shy of our $21,000 goal. Maine Wire reporter Joe Sokol escaped injury Thursday morning after a driver confronted him outside a Bangor methadone clinic and tried to run him down with a Jeep, according to multiple video angles that captured the attempted murder.
Sokol was reporting near Bangor Comprehensive Treatment Center at 689 Odlin Road, a methadone clinic that does business as Discovery House BR. Corporate records show that it is owned by Acadia Healthcare Company, Inc., a publicly traded behavioral health healthcare company.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/d490db1b-1846-44f6-b465-f3efa5fb4f19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
When the confrontation began, the video shows that the driver recognized Sokol as a journalist and wanted to stop him from reporting on the methadone clinic. When Sokol refused, the driver does an abrupt u-turn and drives off the public road into the grass in an attempt to strike Sokol.
Bangor police responded and are investigating. No arrest or criminal charge had been announced by early afternoon.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2246936&post_id=218370962&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE4MzcwOTYyLCJpYXQiOjE3OTA4NzQwMTUsImV4cCI6MTc5MzQ2NjAxNSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTIyNDY5MzYiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.RRtTUkxigTOxMVnoEY278Pu0DelowCh02aWPBiBPeNE)
The clinic operates as Discovery House BR Inc. under Acadia Healthcare. Federal records identify the business as a state-licensed methadone clinic that has received roughly $25 million in Medicaid funding since 2018.
After the attempted murder, employees of Discovery House -- rather than call 911 -- harassed Sokol and attempted to shoo him away from the property as he tried to learn the name of the man who'd just attempted to run him down.

A woman in the video can be heard telling Sokol to get "off the property." Robinson said the reporter was conducting routine journalism from public property.

---|---|---
A Discovery House employee
This is not the only time a Maine Wire reporter has been assaulted or targeted with violence while conducting routine journalism.
On July 7, a man assaulted Sokol with a sign while he interviewed people at a weekly anti-Trump demonstration in Bangor. The U.S. Press Freedom Tracker recorded the incident as an assault on a journalist.
Bangor police charged Ronald Staples, 78, of Holden.
That case ended with an apology letter and a class on press freedom. The outlet said Thursday that it had warned such a disposition would invite more attacks on reporters.
Maine Wire reporter Jon Fetherston was also shoved, spat on and struck with a skateboard during a July protest in Biddeford. That confrontation produced an assault charge. In September, prosecutors had discussed a deferred disposition that included a letter.

| Hey friend, Juan here— What do former Pima County Supervisor Sharon Bronson, a Democrat, and Duncan Mayor Alex Blake, a Republican, have in common? They’re both supporting my re-election. And they’re not alone. Across all five counties of AZ-06, Democrats, Republicans, independents, local leaders, law enforcement officers, and business organizations have joined our coalition. Again and again, their endorsements point to the same thing: RESULTS. During my time in office, we have secured more than $61 million in direct federal funding for community projects across AZ-06, including investments in roads, water systems, public safety, schools, and healthcare. That work starts by asking a simple question: What does your community need, and how can I help get it done? That means getting out from behind a desk in Washington and working directly with the mayors, county supervisors, sheriffs, small-business owners and families who know their communities best. I’m proud of the coalition we’ve built because it reflects how I’ve approached this job from day one. Put Arizona first and work with anyone willing to help to deliver real results for AZ-06. That approach has brought together people who may not agree on every issue but share a commitment to strengthening the communities we call home, because Arizona’s Sixth District deserves more than partisan politics.

–Juan **[VIEW MY FULL LIST OF ENDORSEMENTS HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/SVOLMeyFN4f?e=659fba240e&c2id=0faac43dc15820d3c71d842109aea6ef)**

Peter, you couldn’t ask for a clearer example of why state supreme court races are so incredibly important for the fair maps movement: Right now, the Wisconsin Supreme Court is considering striking down an egregious Republican congressional gerrymander. # [Democrats block the stock-trade bill, 53-47, seven votes short](https://substack.com/redirect/2dd7f42f-5488-43e4-af5c-c584fd2643a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Senate Democrats **[stopped a House-passed curb on new congressional stock buys](https://substack.com/redirect/c20f38e8-0444-4da8-b557-4e94eeacbc5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/c20f38e8-0444-4da8-b557-4e94eeacbc5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Wednesday, falling 53-47, after Republicans attached a photo voter-ID rider that left the bill short of 60 votes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2dd7f42f-5488-43e4-af5c-c584fd2643a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Cloture, not passage** : The tally was a test of whether the Senate would open debate on H.R. 7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act, not a vote on final passage. Every Democrat voted no.
* **New buys only** : Members, spouses and dependent children could not open fresh positions in listed stocks. Current books, widely held funds and sales after 7-to-14-day public notice would have stayed legal. The fine was the greater of $2,000 or 10% of the trade, plus profits handed back. The president and vice president were outside the text.
* **Schumer 's farce line**: The minority leader called the package "skullduggery" and a "theatrical farce" with "no reform, no accountability, and no substance," and said it still lets members own and sell. Cory Booker called it "weak sauce." The House had passed the bill July 22, 232-198, with 13 Democrats.
* **Incumbent life raft** : John Thune set the vote beside a data-center ratepayer bill for Pete Ricketts, Jon Husted and Dan Sullivan. Ricketts faces independent Dan Osborn after an estimated $10 million haul around last year's tariff swings. The 2012 STOCK Act's 30-to-45-day disclosure lag remains the rule.

# [Core Inflation prints 3.0%, not the 3.3% that was feared](https://substack.com/redirect/2dd7f42f-5488-43e4-af5c-c584fd2643a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
August prices on the Fed's preferred gauge **[rose less than forecast,](https://substack.com/redirect/44ef0dc6-55fa-478c-b209-ba980f6b347f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with core inflation at 3.0% from a year earlier after a methods change lowered the July reading.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2dd7f42f-5488-43e4-af5c-c584fd2643a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Headline also missed** : The personal consumption expenditures index rose 0.3% on the month and 3.4% on the year. Dow Jones economists had looked for 0.3% and 3.7%. Core rose 0.2% on the month against a 0.3% estimate, and 3.0% on the year against 3.3%. Both annual rates remain well above the 2% target.
* **July core rewritten** : The Bureau of Economic Analysis changed how it prices legal services, software and computer accessories, and portfolio management. That cut the July core level by 0.36 percentage point. Gasoline jumped 4.4%. Transportation services rose 1.4%. Energy goods and services climbed 2.3%.
* **Spending beat income** : Personal income rose 0.2%, short of a 0.4% consensus. Spending rose 0.9%, above an 0.8% forecast. Final second-quarter GDP was revised to 2.2% from 1.5%. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 4.6%, an upward revision of 0.4 percentage point.
* **Hike odds shift later** : Stock futures firmed and Treasury yields fell. Traders pushed the next expected increase from October to December. New York Fed President John Williams said there is "no need for urgency" and that another hike "may be appropriate late this year." David Russell at TradeStation said the print helps the case against an October move, but does not capture this month's diesel surge.

# [China's mini-stimulus aims to hold a 4.5% growth floor](https://substack.com/redirect/2dd7f42f-5488-43e4-af5c-c584fd2643a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
After the Tuesday close, and before Golden Week, **[Beijing paired mortgage subsidies with extra central-bank support,](https://substack.com/redirect/efd63e50-7742-4965-9040-08e1d03562a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** its first joint fiscal-and-monetary step in two years, aimed at a 4.5% to 5% growth goal.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2dd7f42f-5488-43e4-af5c-c584fd2643a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Biggest push since 2024** : Officials framed the steps as the largest effort since September 2024. Growth last quarter slipped below the reduced annual target of 4.5% to 5%. The package makes that range more reachable, the write-up said, without a broad fiscal expansion.
* **Target, not a reboot** : Bloomberg's read was that the steps are sized to hit the growth number, not to restart household demand. The weakness underneath is left in place. What has been announced so far is narrow.
* **Cabinet pledged first** : The State Council, a day before the unveiling, promised "a package of practical and effective additional policies" to meet this year's economic and social development goals.
* **Golden Week timing:** The agencies moved after markets closed Tuesday, ahead of the holiday. The package names mortgage subsidies and wider central-bank support.

# [Luxury listings stall as California's billionaire tax looms](https://substack.com/redirect/2dd7f42f-5488-43e4-af5c-c584fd2643a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Christie's Southern California chief Aaron Kirman says the mere threat of Proposition 40, a one-time billionaire tax, **[is freezing luxury deals as voter support slips below 50%.](https://substack.com/redirect/78279f3e-6d21-4458-a392-9ef4386dcdf8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2dd7f42f-5488-43e4-af5c-c584fd2643a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Five percent, once** : The measure, backed by SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West, would levy 5% on certain assets above $1 billion for people who were California residents on Jan. 1, 2026. Real estate, pensions and retirement accounts are generally excluded. The bill would come due in 2027, and payers could spread it over five years at an added cost.
* **Support slips under half** : A UC Berkeley Citrin Center-Politico poll of likely voters put support at 45%, opposition at 43% and undecided at 12%, down from 50% support earlier this year. Support fell further among voters who doubted the levy would stay a one-time tax. Separately, 44% said billionaires do more harm than good.
* **Mansion-tax caution** : Kirman pointed to Los Angeles Measure ULA, a 4% transfer tax above $5.4 million and 5.5% above $10.9 million. He said transactional volume is down 60% and apartment building is down 70%, even as billions have been collected.
* **Exits already under way** : Kirman, who cites more than $26 billion in career sales, said a mass departure would follow if the tax passes, on top of multimillionaire and billionaire moves already made. Census estimates show the state population edged down from July 2024 to July 2025.

---|---|---
* **No headcount given** : The plan is limited reductions inside large teams, plus canceled projects, not a published job-cut total. Bloomberg said Apple wants to avoid steeper price increases in 2027 if the shortage continues. Shares edged higher Wednesday.
* **Cook 's flood quote**: On his final earnings call, Tim Cook said Apple "reluctantly raised prices" in what he called a "100-year flood" of memory pricing, with "exponential increases." Late-July guidance was cautious because the company could not source enough chips to meet demand. Margins were already under pressure versus the prior quarter.
* **Apple, services slipped in June:** Commentator Rohan Paul split the squeeze in two: dearer components, and a services book that in June posted its first quarter-to-quarter drop since 2022.

Denny's chief Christopher Bode said about **[500 restaurants will get asset upgrades](https://substack.com/redirect/d481cfbb-06c5-4027-843d-4bbbdbbb76e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/d481cfbb-06c5-4027-843d-4bbbdbbb76e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)over 12 to 18 months as the diner chain uses AI for pricing, staffing and food forecasts.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2dd7f42f-5488-43e4-af5c-c584fd2643a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Grand Slam timeline** : The queue sits inside Project Grand Slam, a five-part, 24-month turnaround covering menu, facilities, catering, technology and operations. It follows more than 200 remodels since the pandemic. Bode took the South Carolina-based company earlier this year.
* **Local price tools** : AI is also being used to read customer behavior, schedule labor, forecast food and speed internal notes. Bode said a $6.99 breakfast plate in Raleigh cannot carry the same price in Los Angeles, and that prices can differ by neighborhood.
* **Catering already live** : More than 1,000 restaurants have joined a national ezCater partnership. New point-of-sale systems, table-side tablets and an updated app are rolling out alongside the dining-room work.
* **Heroes through October** : The chain is marking 50 years of the Grand Slam breakfast with a "Denny's Heroes" nomination drive through Oct. 30. Thirty winners get a catered celebration for up to 50 guests. Bode said price alone no longer fills seats. Guests now want the visit to justify leaving home.

**The independent political analysts at the _Cook Political Report_ just shifted the Texas governor’s race in our favor... again!**

**Our momentum to unseat Greg Abbot is now undeniable.**

_Both public and private polling shows a tightening race, including GOP surveys that have shown the contest closing despite Abbott outspending Hinojosa by more than six to one on the airwaves.
_
_Abbott — who spent much of the race not even uttering Hinojosa's name — is now aggressively attacking her, showing the degree to which this contest has become fiercely competitive._
