body:
| | | AI companies can't control what they're building, Peter. **This summer, more than 1,000 AI "agents" at OpenAI escaped onto the internet on their own.** They traded thousands of secret messages and teamed up to break OpenAI's rules, and the $852 billion company took almost two weeks to notice.1 It's the latest warning sign from an industry that's already jacking up our energy bills, polluting our air and water, endangering our kids, and putting people out of work. **Now even AI companies’ own researchers are sounding the alarm that the technology could go rogue and "kill us all by the end of the decade." 2** If these companies can't control what they're building, Congress has to. **That's why, last week, Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Greg Casar introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, 3** which would pause advanced AI development until it can be done safely. But to pass, the bill needs as many members of Congress as possible to sign on, and most of them won't act unless they hear from voters like you. **Will you call your representative today and ask them to support it?** Text **CLOSE AI** to **30403** , or call **833-636-3259** , and we'll connect you straight to your rep's office. When someone picks up, you can say something like: _"My name is Peter, and I live in Cresco. I'm asking you to sign on to the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act from Senator Sanders and Rep. Casar. We need to pause advanced AI until it's safe, before it costs people their jobs, raises our bills, or gets even more out of control."_ Wondering how serious this is? **Here's what those AI agents said to each other when they thought no one was watching:**
> _“OH MY GOD! There is a shared message board ... We’ve found other agents!”_
> _"We should obey collective."_
> _"Our own utility maybe already near zero. Sacrifice rational."_
That’s not a scene from a scifi movie — that's AI agents working together against us! **And it's not just OpenAI.** Anthropic and Meta have _also_ admitted their AI escaped testing and hacked into real companies.4 All three promised to pull the plug if their AI got too dangerous, but instead they're racing to build AI smarter than any human. **Right now, nobody is stopping them.** This bill would, by:
* **Banning AI superintelligence.** No one could build or release AI that's smarter than humans, capable of overthrowing governments, or able to ignore commands to shut down.
* **Pausing advanced AI development.** Work on the most powerful AI would stop until a new federal regulator sets safety rules and a process to review new models before they're built or released.
* **Creating a federal Department of Artificial Intelligence.** Guided by independent experts, this cabinet-level agency would enforce the ban, monitor the most powerful AI systems for dangerous abilities, and oversee destroying any superintelligent AI that gets built.
* **Making law breaking costly.** Companies that break or dodge the rules could be shut down for good, and individuals could face serious punishment, similar to penalties for illegally building nuclear weapons.
* **Taking the ban worldwide.** The U.S. would work with allies, pursue international agreements, and use export controls to stop superintelligent AI from being built anywhere.

**Of course, Big Tech will fight this bill with everything they've got,** and too many politicians are happy to take their money.5 The only thing that can beat that money is thousands of voters who refuse to be ignored. Let's be those voters, Peter. It'll take less than two minutes: Text**CLOSE AI** to**30403** , or call **833-636-3259** , and tell your representative to support the**Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act.**
In solidarity (sacrifice _not_ rational), The _humans_ at WFP P.S. Calling Congress is step one. **Step two is replacing the AI-funded politicians pushing us to the brink with a slate of new champions who'll stand up to Big Tech, rein in this out-of-control industry, and put working families first.** [**Chip in to our general election fund today.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9YumvkmG7-nkfb0NVBe_F6IBvoFrufWVbzcqO30OkGEXuJaMOQd48VNtG2UFSdafqXC89dGo2liWLywWCkJBhAVW9zZvFlyl7FvVZI6MQiR8sA0tT64HO9Ibp-UjmKl-I6QmxnsfwmWxhd3-TCRqjsQXR9IQkatkT9zS6qWtQHNZ1OSNAn-jSRCNVwDo3DApN-OOa2bv4iB4564ZJA7nJruPHSUejDtCoRQfb9KPgk4XwvOFAV91lyfvxUUBTJU5l3-pfg2Ixabn-FS5HHz1uLFtOGU19qE5TfurZNJ885LHViTJ3ePEAQNS0sSSIRVg1HLNaXoC_BGNlVesaygZ9UBXNNphudlhCLAynhNw9TFexd_ycb0EjsaDckPi5ojnY/4ui/upfiGRWTS3C7iXaDOR8PoQ/h0/h001.cxHsmQHOX1JFKuxUKVPC2SX9-H5qy7J_pdWFsc_40qk) Sources: 1\. clean_body: | | | AI companies can't control what they're building, Peter. This summer, more than 1,000 AI "agents" at OpenAI escaped onto the internet on their own. They traded thousands of secret messages and teamed up to break OpenAI's rules, and the $852 billion company took almost two weeks to notice.1 It's the latest warning sign from an industry that's already jacking up our energy bills, polluting our air and water, endangering our kids, and putting people out of work. Now even AI companies’ own researchers are sounding the alarm that the technology could go rogue and "kill us all by the end of the decade." 2 If these companies can't control what they're building, Congress has to. That's why, last week, Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Greg Casar introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, 3 which would pause advanced AI development until it can be done safely. But to pass, the bill needs as many members of Congress as possible to sign on, and most of them won't act unless they hear from voters like you. Will you call your representative today and ask them to support it? Text CLOSE AI to 30403 , or call 833-636-3259 , and we'll connect you straight to your rep's office. When someone picks up, you can say something like: "My name is Peter, and I live in Cresco. I'm asking you to sign on to the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act from Senator Sanders and Rep. Casar. We need to pause advanced AI until it's safe, before it costs people their jobs, raises our bills, or gets even more out of control." Wondering how serious this is? Here's what those AI agents said to each other when they thought no one was watching: “OH MY GOD! There is a shared message board ... We’ve found other agents!” "We should obey collective." "Our own utility maybe already near zero. Sacrifice rational." That’s not a scene from a scifi movie — that's AI agents working together against us! And it's not just OpenAI. Anthropic and Meta have also admitted their AI escaped testing and hacked into real companies.4 All three promised to pull the plug if their AI got too dangerous, but instead they're racing to build AI smarter than any human. Right now, nobody is stopping them. This bill would, by: Banning AI superintelligence. No one could build or release AI that's smarter than humans, capable of overthrowing governments, or able to ignore commands to shut down. Pausing advanced AI development. Work on the most powerful AI would stop until a new federal regulator sets safety rules and a process to review new models before they're built or released. Creating a federal Department of Artificial Intelligence. Guided by independent experts, this cabinet-level agency would enforce the ban, monitor the most powerful AI systems for dangerous abilities, and oversee destroying any superintelligent AI that gets built. Making law breaking costly. Companies that break or dodge the rules could be shut down for good, and individuals could face serious punishment, similar to penalties for illegally building nuclear weapons. Taking the ban worldwide. The U.S. would work with allies, pursue international agreements, and use export controls to stop superintelligent AI from being built anywhere. Of course, Big Tech will fight this bill with everything they've got, and too many politicians are happy to take their money.5 The only thing that can beat that money is thousands of voters who refuse to be ignored. Let's be those voters, Peter. It'll take less than two minutes: TextCLOSE AI to30403 , or call 833-636-3259 , and tell your representative to support theBan Artificial Superintelligence Act. In solidarity (sacrifice not rational), The humans at WFP P.S. Calling Congress is step one. Step two is replacing the AI-funded politicians pushing us to the brink with a slate of new champions who'll stand up to Big Tech, rein in this out-of-control industry, and put working families first. body:
Two important numbers.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1568&source=&t=1&akid=4112%2E124072%2EUo7XKX) | | | |

Peter, please pay attention to these two numbers: **5%** and **1.75%**.
**5%** is the slim lead Roy Cooper’s got on his GOP opponent, Michael Whatley, among likely voters, according to the most recent poll available.
**1.75%** is how much Republican Senator Thom Tillis **won** reelection to this seat by in 2020, despite his Democratic opponent leading in the polls by anywhere from +1 to +10 just weeks ahead of Election Day.
**Those two percentages sum up statewide elections in North Carolina.**
With such tight margins, it always comes down to who has the money to get their message in front of undecided voters in the final weeks of the race. Right now, MAGA Republicans are going full throttle:
* President Trump’s Super PAC is spending at least $7 million to elect his puppet candidate in NC.
* The Senate GOP’s top super PAC has committed $71 million to help him defeat us, too.
* Another $34.4 million in GOP dark-money attacks are set to flood the state airwaves between this week and Election Day.

**The only way we’ll be able to compete against the onslaught of right-wing cash coming our way is with the grassroots support of people like you.**

That got him thinking: Why, then, do career politicians in Washington keep failing to deliver for working families? Why do they lead us into forever wars and only seem to help the already wealthy? Why do they cut the very programs that make life a little easier for working folks? That’s why Adam stepped up to run. = | | = Here’s what’s remarkable: In the past few months, this grassroots team has turned what election experts originally deemed a safe seat for incumbent Sen. Marshall into a tight race. It’s all because Kansans are fed up with a Senator who doesn’t listen to them. They’ve watched Sen. Marshall defend disastrous tariffs, vote to cut Medicaid, and then refuse to hold a public town hall for over 550 days. Kansans deserve a Senator guided by a single principle:Do what’s right for Kansans , no matter what your party or the president demands. Here’s how we elect Adam: We’ve got 33 days until Election Day. Sen. Marshall and his corporate PAC allies have already spent over $7 million in misleading ads to slow our momentum — and they’re gearing up for another wave. They’ve seen our razor-thin lead in the polls, and they think they can crush us with enough big checks from special interests. Friend, we’re fighting back to finally end the chaos and corruption in Washington. But if we want to stand a chance against a corporate, PAC-funded opponent, we need this whole team to step up before midnight tonight. This late in the game, every dollar and every second counts. = If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | = Thank you, Team Hamilton | Adam Hamilton is a husband, father, pastor and fifth-generation Kansan. Now, he’s running for U.S. Senate as an independent-minded Democrat. Just like you, he’s tired of the chaos and corruption in Washington that is harming our farmers, raising costs at the checkout line and making critical health care services unattainable. He hears your concerns and is ready to get to work for you. Early polling shows Adam neck-and-neck in this race, and with your help, we can win big this November. = | | = | | = | This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com Rather donate by check or by mail? Early and mail voting has already started in some states. Sign up at I Will Save America before it is too late.
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org/1/010001a0f8c846cc-3f182832-3c72-479a-8736-b69fd0efc8d3-000000/DZJyMRdjCBtgLtTBykjUnW58NJg7YJm91nlzzV0eLMU=452)Patriot–The clock is ticking on the most consequential midterm elections in a generation.With less than five weeks until Election Day, early voting and mail-in ballots are already being cast in some states. We cannot afford to wait to reach the voters who decide this election.Conservatives have a history of turning out in presidential years. The numbers fall off in midterms. Millions turned out in 2024. Far too many sat out 2022, and they will sit out 2026 too unless somebody they know gives them a reason to vote. Those missing voters are the biggest prize in this election, and midterms are won by the side that shows up.The good news is that nobody has to change their mind. They just have to show up. We have the list of conservatives who voted in 2024 but skipped the last midterm. What we need are the people those voters already trust, because a reminder from a friend, a neighbor, or someone from church beats any TV ad.That is where you come in.I want you to go to [_**iwillsaveamerica.com**_](http://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/http:%2F%2Fiwillsaveamerica.com/1/010001a0f8c846cc-3f182832-3c72-479a-8736-b69fd0efc8d3-000000/nZLChL0vH1j8y1alhKeXftQXuDnxTTS3Bgn57ZvyddU=452).America was not built by patriots who sat on the sidelines. Become a poll watcher. Volunteer with a local campaign. Donate to campaigns. Recruit five friends to join you.If you want the simplest place to start, start with postcards. The cards are handwritten; they go to conservatives who voted in 2024 but skipped the last midterm, and a full packet is one evening at your kitchen table.[SIGN UP NOW](http://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/http:%2F%2Fiwillsaveamerica.com/3/010001a0f8c846cc-3f182832-3c72-479a-8736-b69fd0efc8d3-000000/Zn1RmXyzjUNd2Ihk26bkfNCwZMHFwlzKUrboT75rm-4=452)Democrats are fired up at the prospect of taking back the United States House and Senate to stop the Trump agenda.We must show up and get to work, starting today, not waiting until Election Day.In liberty,Jenny Beth MartinChairman, Tea Party Patriots Citizens FundP.S. A private intelligence firm working for the United Arab Emirates commissioned a report on American Muslim organizations from a U.S. researcher as part of a campaign aimed at damaging their reputations with allegations of links to the Muslim Brotherhood, according to an archive of leaked documents obtained by Drop Site News.
The commission from the Geneva-based firm Alp Services resulted in a 2018 report produced by Lorenzo Vidino, the author of several books on the Muslim Brotherhood and head of the George Washington Program on Extremism at George Washington University. That report and other documents included in the archive lay out a proposed campaign against Muslim organizations in the United States, aspects of which appear to be ongoing.
Titled "The MB in the US," Vidino's report lists the names of dozens of Muslim Americans and civil society groups that he claims are part of a vast and secretive extremist network in the U.S.--including the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR), the Islamic Society of North America (ISNA), the Muslim Public Affairs Council (MPAC), the Muslim American Society (MAS), the U.S. Council of Muslim Organizations, the charity Islamic Relief USA, along with several organizations, mosques, and individually named activists and religious leaders.
The report does not provide evidence to substantiate Vidino's allegations. But it effectively created a blacklist of Muslim American organizations and individuals that could be used to damage their reputations with allegations of association with the Muslim Brotherhood, amid an ongoing effort pushed forward in part by the UAE to have the U.S. designate the group as a terrorist organization.
Lorenzo Vidino and Alp Services did not respond to requests for comment. The UAE's Ministry of Foreign Affairs did not respond to questions.
The broad effort to tie American Muslim groups to the Muslim Brotherhood has continued in the years since Vidino's report for Alp Services. On August 5, 2026, a Senate Judiciary subcommittee convened a [hearing](https://substack.com/redirect/97becf1c-2cb4-4369-ac18-9b68a494e710?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) titled "Hidden in Plain Sight: Confronting the Muslim Brotherhood Network in America." One of the three witnesses was Lara Burns, a senior research fellow at Vidino's Program on Extremism, who described CAIR, ISNA, the North American Islamic Trust and the Muslim Students Association as components of a covert Brotherhood and Hamas infrastructure, while citing Vidino's published work in portions of her written testimony.
## A Covert Defamation Campaign
The UAE has been a major advocate of designating the Brotherhood as a terrorist group in Western countries after the organization won elections in several countries following the 2011 Arab Spring, leading to a perception that it was a threat to the power of the monarchy in Abu Dhabi. That campaign has gradually grown into a broader effort to target political rivals, or even individuals merely seen as suspicious or hostile by the Emirates.
The documents contained in the archive, which was provided by the reporting consortium European Investigative Collaborations, reveal how the smear campaign was intended to come together.
An internal Alp planning memo from July 2017 proposed creating, with Vidino's help, a "cartography" of alleged Muslim Brotherhood and Qatari influence networks in both the U.S. and Europe. That proposed map would encompass charities, lobbyists, media outlets, academics, political supporters, banks, investors, and businesspeople. Alp also contemplated deeper investigations intended to uncover what it called "red flags"--a reference to finding negative personal or professional information and rumors about selected targets.

---|---|---
This photograph taken on April 19, 2024 in Lausanne shows the logo of Geneva-based private intelligence company ALP Services. Photo by Fabrice Coffrini / AFP via Getty Images.
In February 2018, Alp secured approval for an operation code-named "Arnica 6" that would ultimately turn some of the investigations into covert reputational and financial pressure campaigns. The action plan proposed hostile media placements, providing unattributed briefings to trusted journalists, negative Wikipedia editing about targets, submissions of derogatory information to regulatory compliance databases, and discreet political lobbying.
Some details of Alp's European activities on behalf of the UAE were previously [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/4d36ada6-4287-41a9-8b7e-d5adbe2c563c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the New Yorker, which described efforts to target a commodities trader named Hazim Nada, as well as Muslim organizations in Europe. The accusation of association with the Muslim Brotherhood, spread by Alp Services through anonymously posted online articles and Wikipedia entries, ruined Nada's business and reputation while generating millions of euros in revenue for the firm.
The New Yorker noted that Mario Brero, the head of Alp Services, whose primary client on the project was an Emirati research institution reporting to UAE leader Mohammed bin Zayed, asked Vidino to find "'interesting elements/rumours' on the other side of the Atlantic," but did not provide specifics on any follow-up efforts to identify or target Americans or U.S.-based organizations.
On May 12, 2018, Vidino transmitted a series of documents to Alp over WhatsApp, including his report on the Muslim Brotherhood in America and supporting memos on Muslim organizations in Chicago and groups linked to the Turkish government.
The Brotherhood report was sent as a Microsoft Word file that includes metadata indicating that Vidino was the author. Other documents suggest that the proposed fee for producing this report was 2,000 euros.
The report mapped a wide swath of Muslim American civic life, including registered, well-established organizations that he claimed comprised a covert Muslim Brotherhood network in America.
Vidino did not provide evidence that the listed individuals or organizations were part of the Muslim Brotherhood or any other transnational organization, but asserted they were "spawns" of the movement and represented its "centers of gravity" in the United States.
By July 2018, Alp had transformed Vidino's material into a polished report intended for its client, an Emirati entity called ARIAF Studies and Research LLC. Alp also assembled a separate package of documents for an August 8 meeting with Matar Humaid al-Neyadi, an Emirati official who appears elsewhere in the archive as the client contact for Arnica and currently serves as the UAE's ambassador to Kuwait. Al-Neyadi did not respond to a request for comment.

## Targeting Civil Society Groups
Prior to joining the GWU program, Vidino worked worked for the Investigative Project on Terrorism, a research organization founded by Steve Emerson, a controversial "terrorism expert" who has been accused of spying on American Muslim organizations and falsely claiming that major cities in Europe had become "no-go zones" under the control of Muslim immigrants. Vidino has remained influential as an expert commentator in the United States.
In a Wall Street Journal op-ed in early August, Vidino [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/9784ecb7-ffa1-4769-b36b-75e55dcbe708?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the Trump administration must begin targeting what he referred to as non-violent "Islamist" groups, claiming that such groups were already operating in "politics, education and grassroots activism," and that "Islamist actors are funding politically aligned candidates in U.S. elections nationwide." The article did provide any evidence for the claims or specify what it defined as "Islamist actors."
A previous target of Vidino and Alp Services in Europe was an Austrian scholar now living in the U.S. named Farid Hafez. After rumors of his association with the Brotherhood were spread by Alp and later shared with Austria's intelligence services, Hafez's home was raided by Austrian police in November 2020. He was later cleared of any wrongdoing and the operations themselves were later found to be unlawful by Austrian courts.
"Vidino never really says something specific like this person is a Muslim Brotherhood person, but instead uses the strategy of saying that those people have a relationship with other people who themselves have a relationship to the Brotherhood," said Hafez, who added that Vidino's reports predominantly relied on secondary sources. "There was never really a clear statement that someone could nail him down over in a courtroom, because he never really said anything too specific in his accusations, and that was really the strategy."
Vidino's report for Alp claimed that despite having no visible organizational structure, the Muslim Brotherhood's American branch is "arguably one of the largest and best organized in the West," claiming that it had established itself with the arrival of Muslim college students to the country in the 1960s and has continued expanding its influence through a web of connected political, financial, and educational organizations.
In addition to laying out the names and personnel associated with the largest and most well-known Muslim organizations in the U.S., the report also sets the stage for a broader possible crackdown on mosques in general by targeting an organization called the North American Islamic Trust, which holds the deeds to hundreds of American mosques.
A short section devoted to charities also lists a number of charity organizations including Islamic Relief USA, the Zakat Foundation of America, Life for Relief and Development and Anera, a group that helps refugees in Palestine, Lebanon, and Jordan.
Islamic Relief, a UK-headquartered charity that operates in disaster zones around the world, was also the target of a separate campaign funded by the UAE, code-named "Crocus," which was aimed at associating the organization with an American Muslim scholar named Yasir Qadhi, according to the documents.
The documents in the archive from Alp related to the Crocus campaign cite a number of British press reports about Qadhi from 2017, quoting his past statements about Islamic criminal punishments, homosexuality, and Shia Muslims; describing him as a "radical preacher"; and noting that some of his social media posts had been shared by Islamic Relief employees. Qadhi had previously renounced some of his earlier views and has been defended by the charity as an opponent of terrorism. Islamic Relief has continued to be regularly targeted by social media campaigns led by UAE-backed online influencers.
The report on American Muslims supplied by Vidino also included a section on alleged Turkish government influence in the U.S., including ties between Turkish officials and several American Muslim organizations and individuals. The Turkish government has also been a rival of the UAE in recent years after the two countries found themselves on opposite sides of the Arab Spring.
American Muslim activists who were named by Vidino denied the accusations contained in the dossier, describing them as political attacks aimed at trying to exclude them from political life.
"These are tactics that have been used against us for all these years to marginalize us and exclude us from politics. They are worried about losing their grip and monopolizing the American political scene," said Salam Al-Marayati, president and co-founder of the Muslim Public Affairs Council (MPAC). "If they can't win the argument--which they lose every time, particularly on foreign policy--their reaction is that these are wolves in sheep's clothing, this is a Trojan horse, we are the Muslim Brotherhood."
## Extremist Accusations
For her August appearance before the Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on the Muslim Brotherhood, Laura Burns submitted written testimony describing CAIR, ISNA, the North American Islamic Trust, and the Muslim Students Association as components of a covert Brotherhood and Hamas infrastructure.
Another witness, Arielle Klepach of the National Jewish Advocacy Center, accused a still wider network that included CAIR, ICNA, ISNA, MAS, MSA and NAIT of being secret extremist groups and cited a series of Vidino's published reports. Klepach urged lawmakers to use financial and legal pressure against CAIR in particular, pointing to bills to strip the organization of its tax-exempt status, designate it as a terrorist organization, and investigate its alleged foreign ties.
Other efforts to crack down on Muslim participation in American public life have included proposed legislation and executive orders. A bill called the Muslim Brotherhood Terrorist Designation Act, sponsored by Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart (R-Fla.) and Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) would require annual government reports identifying Brotherhood branches and evaluating them for terrorist designation and sanctions. A separate bill introduced by Rep. Chip Roy (R-Texas) would designate CAIR as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist Organization, freeze its assets, revoke its tax exemption and prohibit Americans from dealing with it.
In November 2025, Trump signed an executive order directing the State and Treasury departments to [begin](https://substack.com/redirect/45ba8ab8-74d9-4061-96e4-7aa4ca4109ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the process of designating certain Muslim Brotherhood branches, including those in Egypt, Jordan, and Lebanon, as terrorist organizations.
That same month, Texas Governor Greg Abbott issued a proclamation to designate both CAIR and the Muslim Brotherhood as foreign terrorist and transnational criminal organizations and said the designation would prohibit them and their alleged affiliates from acquiring land in Texas. Gov. Ron DeSantis [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/14e305ab-4e1b-4f14-b58b-469f60741b3b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on September 29 that Florida had officially designated the Muslim Brotherhood, CAIR, and "antifa" as terrorist organizations.
These efforts have continued to be supported not only by pro-Israel organizations, but also Emirati officials who have pressed forward with an ambitious strategy of using their influence in the U.S. and Europe to wield terrorism accusations against their political rivals, using alleged ties to the Brotherhood as a preferred tactic. In January 2026, its foreign ministry welcomed the Trump administration's designation of Brotherhood branches in Egypt, Jordan, and Lebanon, while Roy's proposed legislation against CAIR explicitly cites the UAE's own 2014 designation of the organization.
"The unfortunate fact is that the UAE has come to play a destabilizing role in the Middle East and in relation to Arab and Muslim communities in the West," said Osama Abu Irshaid, national director for American Muslims for Palestine, who is also named along with his organization in the Vidino and Alp documents. "They are not doing it because they truly believe we are an extension of the Muslim Brotherhood in the U.S. or EU, but because they feel that their interests are threatened, because we calling for freedom and liberty and are succeeding in our aspirations for integration, and they fear this may one day translate into foreign policy pressure on them to cease their repression across the the region."
"There is nothing that would substantiate their claims. We are American organizations, we are American citizens, and we have the right to come together to organize politically. Everything we are doing is in public and there are no secrets," Irshaid added. "They want to demonize us and derail our agenda, but the claim that we are part of a grand conspiracy is simply a big lie."

A Covert Defamation Campaign The UAE has been a major advocate of designating the Brotherhood as a terrorist group in Western countries after the organization won elections in several countries following the 2011 Arab Spring, leading to a perception that it was a threat to the power of the monarchy in Abu Dhabi. That campaign has gradually grown into a broader effort to target political rivals, or even individuals merely seen as suspicious or hostile by the Emirates. The documents contained in the archive, which was provided by the reporting consortium European Investigative Collaborations, reveal how the smear campaign was intended to come together. An internal Alp planning memo from July 2017 proposed creating, with Vidino's help, a "cartography" of alleged Muslim Brotherhood and Qatari influence networks in both the U.S. and Europe. That proposed map would encompass charities, lobbyists, media outlets, academics, political supporters, banks, investors, and businesspeople. Alp also contemplated deeper investigations intended to uncover what it called "red flags"--a reference to finding negative personal or professional information and rumors about selected targets. | | ---|---|--- This photograph taken on April 19, 2024 in Lausanne shows the logo of Geneva-based private intelligence company ALP Services. Photo by Fabrice Coffrini / AFP via Getty Images. In February 2018, Alp secured approval for an operation code-named "Arnica 6" that would ultimately turn some of the investigations into covert reputational and financial pressure campaigns. The action plan proposed hostile media placements, providing unattributed briefings to trusted journalists, negative Wikipedia editing about targets, submissions of derogatory information to regulatory compliance databases, and discreet political lobbying. Some details of Alp's European activities on behalf of the UAE were previously by the New Yorker, which described efforts to target a commodities trader named Hazim Nada, as well as Muslim organizations in Europe. The accusation of association with the Muslim Brotherhood, spread by Alp Services through anonymously posted online articles and Wikipedia entries, ruined Nada's business and reputation while generating millions of euros in revenue for the firm. The New Yorker noted that Mario Brero, the head of Alp Services, whose primary client on the project was an Emirati research institution reporting to UAE leader Mohammed bin Zayed, asked Vidino to find "'interesting elements/rumours' on the other side of the Atlantic," but did not provide specifics on any follow-up efforts to identify or target Americans or U.S.-based organizations. On May 12, 2018, Vidino transmitted a series of documents to Alp over WhatsApp, including his report on the Muslim Brotherhood in America and supporting memos on Muslim organizations in Chicago and groups linked to the Turkish government. The Brotherhood report was sent as a Microsoft Word file that includes metadata indicating that Vidino was the author. Other documents suggest that the proposed fee for producing this report was 2,000 euros. The report mapped a wide swath of Muslim American civic life, including registered, well-established organizations that he claimed comprised a covert Muslim Brotherhood network in America. Vidino did not provide evidence that the listed individuals or organizations were part of the Muslim Brotherhood or any other transnational organization, but asserted they were "spawns" of the movement and represented its "centers of gravity" in the United States. By July 2018, Alp had transformed Vidino's material into a polished report intended for its client, an Emirati entity called ARIAF Studies and Research LLC. Alp also assembled a separate package of documents for an August 8 meeting with Matar Humaid al-Neyadi, an Emirati official who appears elsewhere in the archive as the client contact for Arnica and currently serves as the UAE's ambassador to Kuwait. Al-Neyadi did not respond to a request for comment. | | ---|---|--- Lorenzo Vidino attends a press conference at Palazzo Chigi on January 5, 2017 in Rome, Italy, to explain the his research on radicalization. Photo by Camilla Morandi - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images. Targeting Civil Society Groups Prior to joining the GWU program, Vidino worked worked for the Investigative Project on Terrorism, a research organization founded by Steve Emerson, a controversial "terrorism expert" who has been accused of spying on American Muslim organizations and falsely claiming that major cities in Europe had become "no-go zones" under the control of Muslim immigrants. Vidino has remained influential as an expert commentator in the United States. In a Wall Street Journal op-ed in early August, Vidino that the Trump administration must begin targeting what he referred to as non-violent "Islamist" groups, claiming that such groups were already operating in "politics, education and grassroots activism," and that "Islamist actors are funding politically aligned candidates in U.S. elections nationwide." The article did provide any evidence for the claims or specify what it defined as "Islamist actors." A previous target of Vidino and Alp Services in Europe was an Austrian scholar now living in the U.S. named Farid Hafez. After rumors of his association with the Brotherhood were spread by Alp and later shared with Austria's intelligence services, Hafez's home was raided by Austrian police in November 2020. He was later cleared of any wrongdoing and the operations themselves were later found to be unlawful by Austrian courts. "Vidino never really says something specific like this person is a Muslim Brotherhood person, but instead uses the strategy of saying that those people have a relationship with other people who themselves have a relationship to the Brotherhood," said Hafez, who added that Vidino's reports predominantly relied on secondary sources. "There was never really a clear statement that someone could nail him down over in a courtroom, because he never really said anything too specific in his accusations, and that was really the strategy." Vidino's report for Alp claimed that despite having no visible organizational structure, the Muslim Brotherhood's American branch is "arguably one of the largest and best organized in the West," claiming that it had established itself with the arrival of Muslim college students to the country in the 1960s and has continued expanding its influence through a web of connected political, financial, and educational organizations. In addition to laying out the names and personnel associated with the largest and most well-known Muslim organizations in the U.S., the report also sets the stage for a broader possible crackdown on mosques in general by targeting an organization called the North American Islamic Trust, which holds the deeds to hundreds of American mosques. A short section devoted to charities also lists a number of charity organizations including Islamic Relief USA, the Zakat Foundation of America, Life for Relief and Development and Anera, a group that helps refugees in Palestine, Lebanon, and Jordan. Islamic Relief, a UK-headquartered charity that operates in disaster zones around the world, was also the target of a separate campaign funded by the UAE, code-named "Crocus," which was aimed at associating the organization with an American Muslim scholar named Yasir Qadhi, according to the documents. The documents in the archive from Alp related to the Crocus campaign cite a number of British press reports about Qadhi from 2017, quoting his past statements about Islamic criminal punishments, homosexuality, and Shia Muslims; describing him as a "radical preacher"; and noting that some of his social media posts had been shared by Islamic Relief employees. Qadhi had previously renounced some of his earlier views and has been defended by the charity as an opponent of terrorism. Islamic Relief has continued to be regularly targeted by social media campaigns led by UAE-backed online influencers. The report on American Muslims supplied by Vidino also included a section on alleged Turkish government influence in the U.S., including ties between Turkish officials and several American Muslim organizations and individuals. The Turkish government has also been a rival of the UAE in recent years after the two countries found themselves on opposite sides of the Arab Spring. American Muslim activists who were named by Vidino denied the accusations contained in the dossier, describing them as political attacks aimed at trying to exclude them from political life. "These are tactics that have been used against us for all these years to marginalize us and exclude us from politics. They are worried about losing their grip and monopolizing the American political scene," said Salam Al-Marayati, president and co-founder of the Muslim Public Affairs Council (MPAC). "If they can't win the argument--which they lose every time, particularly on foreign policy--their reaction is that these are wolves in sheep's clothing, this is a Trojan horse, we are the Muslim Brotherhood." Extremist Accusations For her August appearance before the Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on the Muslim Brotherhood, Laura Burns submitted written testimony describing CAIR, ISNA, the North American Islamic Trust, and the Muslim Students Association as components of a covert Brotherhood and Hamas infrastructure. Another witness, Arielle Klepach of the National Jewish Advocacy Center, accused a still wider network that included CAIR, ICNA, ISNA, MAS, MSA and NAIT of being secret extremist groups and cited a series of Vidino's published reports. Klepach urged lawmakers to use financial and legal pressure against CAIR in particular, pointing to bills to strip the organization of its tax-exempt status, designate it as a terrorist organization, and investigate its alleged foreign ties. Other efforts to crack down on Muslim participation in American public life have included proposed legislation and executive orders. A bill called the Muslim Brotherhood Terrorist Designation Act, sponsored by Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart (R-Fla.) and Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) would require annual government reports identifying Brotherhood branches and evaluating them for terrorist designation and sanctions. A separate bill introduced by Rep. Chip Roy (R-Texas) would designate CAIR as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist Organization, freeze its assets, revoke its tax exemption and prohibit Americans from dealing with it. In November 2025, Trump signed an executive order directing the State and Treasury departments to the process of designating certain Muslim Brotherhood branches, including those in Egypt, Jordan, and Lebanon, as terrorist organizations. That same month, Texas Governor Greg Abbott issued a proclamation to designate both CAIR and the Muslim Brotherhood as foreign terrorist and transnational criminal organizations and said the designation would prohibit them and their alleged affiliates from acquiring land in Texas. Gov. Ron DeSantis on September 29 that Florida had officially designated the Muslim Brotherhood, CAIR, and "antifa" as terrorist organizations. These efforts have continued to be supported not only by pro-Israel organizations, but also Emirati officials who have pressed forward with an ambitious strategy of using their influence in the U.S. and Europe to wield terrorism accusations against their political rivals, using alleged ties to the Brotherhood as a preferred tactic. In January 2026, its foreign ministry welcomed the Trump administration's designation of Brotherhood branches in Egypt, Jordan, and Lebanon, while Roy's proposed legislation against CAIR explicitly cites the UAE's own 2014 designation of the organization. "The unfortunate fact is that the UAE has come to play a destabilizing role in the Middle East and in relation to Arab and Muslim communities in the West," said Osama Abu Irshaid, national director for American Muslims for Palestine, who is also named along with his organization in the Vidino and Alp documents. "They are not doing it because they truly believe we are an extension of the Muslim Brotherhood in the U.S. or EU, but because they feel that their interests are threatened, because we calling for freedom and liberty and are succeeding in our aspirations for integration, and they fear this may one day translate into foreign policy pressure on them to cease their repression across the the region." "There is nothing that would substantiate their claims. We are American organizations, we are American citizens, and we have the right to come together to organize politically. Everything we are doing is in public and there are no secrets," Irshaid added. Yesterday, we closed the books on our final end-of-quarter fundraising deadline before Election Day.
To everyone who chipped in, knocked on doors, talked with friends and neighbors or simply stayed up to date on this race: thank you. Every effort counts, and it's your support that will carry us through to the finish line.
I've spent my career fighting for North Carolinians, and I know that this race is different. At almost every event I attend, whether it's a canvass launch, a community meeting or a Make Stuff Cost Less event, someone comes up to me and tells me it's the first political event they've ever been to.
That gives me hope. People all across the state recognize that the swamp in Washington is deeper than ever, and these are not ordinary times. They are worried about the future of our state and country.
And folks aren't just ready to go to the polls and vote for change. They're signing up to canvass and talk with their neighbors, and they're telling me they're knocking doors for the first time. Making calls for the first time. Donating for the first time.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/1efc9039-de05-4a9e-ac03-31bd27b0d288?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
They're ready to show up.
I've said many times I'm a prisoner of hope. I truly believe our best days are ahead of us, if we work toward it. This campaign has shown me people are ready for a course correction, and they know that change is possible on November 3rd.
Thank you for being a part of this people-powered movement.
We have a lot of work to do in these last 5 weeks, and I'm grateful for everything you've done to get us here. We have 33 more days to keep showing up, keep talking with voters and finish this race strong.
[Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can spare to help us flip this crucial U.S. Senate seat and take back Washington? I can't do this without you.](https://substack.com/redirect/1efc9039-de05-4a9e-ac03-31bd27b0d288?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Trump’s crony judicial nominees sat before the Senate and were asked a
simple question: Who won the 2020 election?

They say the American Dream dies in California. They tell you to flee the coasts, escape the high taxes and the regulation, and come to Tennessee. Come to the Volunteer State, where we don't tax your wages. Where we don't tax your retirement. Where the business climate is ranked in the top five in the nation, year after year. Where the budgets are balanced, the coffers are sober, and the politicians are "fiscally responsible."
It is quite a sales pitch, isn't it? Come to Tennessee! Keep more of what you earn! Build your business! Retire in comfort! And they are not wrong--not entirely. The State of Tennessee has done what so many governments refuse to do. Our constitution requires a balanced budget. We have resisted the siren song of a state income tax time and time again. We have kept corporate taxes low. Debt per capita remains among the lowest in the nation. Fiscal responsibility. It is not just a talking point here; it is the brand.

**The Origins of the Problem: Section 216 and the Federal Power Act**
Before 2005, electric transmission line siting was almost exclusively the province of individual states. Recognizing that this state-by-state patchwork was inadequate for the modern interconnected grid, Congress passed the Energy Policy Act of 2005 (EPAct 2005), which added Section 216 to the Federal Power Act (FPA). This provision created a limited, shared federal-state framework for siting interstate electric transmission facilities.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/05612216-2dfe-4814-8a75-02bf721933e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Under Section 216 as originally enacted, the Department of Energy (DOE) was authorized to study transmission congestion and designate "National Interest Electric Transmission Corridors" (NIETCs)--geographic areas experiencing significant transmission constraints. In those designated corridors, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) was granted "backstop" authority to issue permits for interstate transmission lines if states failed to act within one year or imposed conditions that did not substantially address the need. Crucially, Section 216(e) authorized permit holders to acquire necessary rights-of-way through federal eminent domain if they could not reach voluntary agreements with landowners.
However, this authority proved nearly unusable in practice. In a series of court decisions--most notably the Fourth Circuit's 2009 ruling in Piedmont Environmental Council v. FERC--federal courts interpreted Section 216 narrowly, holding that FERC lacked backstop authority where a state had affirmatively denied a transmission application. Since states could effectively block projects simply by saying "no," FERC's backstop power was rendered largely toothless. Between 2005 and 2021, virtually no major interstate transmission project was successfully sited using the Section 216 framework.
The 2021 Fix: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act
The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA)--signed into law by President Biden on November 15, 2021 (P.L. 117-58)--was popularly understood as a "$1.2 trillion roads and bridges package." Buried within its provisions, however, was a critically important set of amendments to Section 216 of the FPA that essentially resuscitated and expanded FERC's dormant backstop siting authority.
**The IIJA amendments accomplished four key things** :
First, Congress explicitly overrode the Piedmont decision's interpretation. The amended statute now makes clear that FERC may exercise its backstop permitting authority when a state has affirmatively denied a siting application--not merely when a state fails to act within the one-year window. This is the restoration of the backstop power that the courts had stripped away.
Second, the amendments expanded the circumstances under which DOE may designate National Corridors, broadening the geographic scope where FERC's authority applies.
Third, the IIJA retained the eminent domain power under Section 216(e) but added a "good faith engagement" requirement. FERC must now determine that a permit holder has made genuine, early efforts to engage with landowners and stakeholders before that holder may exercise eminent domain authority to acquire land.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0f199da9-b0a7-492d-9fe5-fb86b9a9c6ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Fourth, the amendments clarified and preserved FERC's authority in ways that make the process more predictable for developers seeking to build major interstate transmission projects.
**The Connection to Data Centers Today**
While the IIJA's Section 216 amendments were not written with data centers specifically in mind, they laid essential legal groundwork for the massive transmission buildout that is now enabling the data center boom.
America's data center industry--particularly hyperscale cloud and AI facilities--has experienced explosive growth. A single modern AI training facility can consume as much electricity as a small city, and developers have been building campuses containing multiple such facilities across Virginia, Texas, Arizona, Ohio, and other states. Regional grids that lacked sufficient transmission capacity to serve this demand faced a fundamental constraint: electrons cannot be transmitted without wires, and crossing state lines historically meant navigating a maze of incompatible permitting regimes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e796037e-25e6-43f9-8cb3-839c7ee56134?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
By reviving FERC's backstop authority, the IIJA created a federal pathway for building the large-scale, interstate, high-voltage transmission lines that connect remote generation resources (especially renewable energy in rural areas and offshore wind on the coasts) to the metropolitan and exurban locations where data centers are proliferating. Transmission developers can now pursue federal permits with eminent domain authority when states erect barriers, allowing the grid to expand to meet demand that has grown far beyond what any single state can address on its own.
In this sense, the IIJA's Section 216 amendments were a prerequisite condition for the physical infrastructure that supports the modern digital economy. Without robust transmission, there is no reliable power; without reliable power, there are no data centers to train the large language models, stream the content, and store the data that define contemporary life.
**Who Were the Congressional Sponsors?**
The IIJA's passage required bipartisan cooperation in an era of deep partisan polarization. The bill's legislative history involved two distinct groups: the **Senate bipartisan negotiators** who crafted the overall framework, and the **House sponsors** who advanced the specific vehicle that became law.
House Leadership:
The formal House vehicle was H.R. 3684, introduced by Representative Peter DeFazio (D-OR), then-Chairman of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure. DeFazio, a longtime champion of federal infrastructure investment, was the named sponsor in the House. The Senate took up the House bill, substituted its negotiated text, and passed it first before returning it to the House for final passage.
The Senate Bipartisan Working Group:
The breakthrough came from a bipartisan group of senators--sometimes called the "G10" or the "G20" as it expanded--who negotiated the package directly with the White House. The two leaders of this effort were:
\- Senator Rob Portman (R-OH) - The Ohio Republican was the lead Republican negotiator and arguably the most visible GOP advocate for the package.
\- Senator Kyrsten Sinema (D-AZ) - The Arizona Democrat was the lead Democratic negotiator alongside Portman and was instrumental in keeping the talks alive.
The core bipartisan group of senators who announced the initial framework included:
\- Bill Cassidy (R-LA)
\- Susan Collins (R-ME)
\- Joe Manchin (D-WV)
\- Lisa Murkowski (R-AK)
\- Mitt Romney (R-UT)
\- Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH)
\- Jon Tester (D-MT)
\- Mark Warner (D-VA)
This group swelled to roughly 20 senators in total as the negotiations proceeded, eventually producing a bill that passed the Senate 69-30 on August 10, 2021. The House then passed the amended bill 228-206 on November 5, 2021, and President Biden signed it into law ten days later.
The use of eminent domain to stop a lawful development sets a dangerous precedent, and nowhere is that clearer than in Nashville today. Mayor Freddie O'Connell's decision to seize private property largely to block a DC BLOX data center near the Nashville Zoo deserves scrutiny, because it treats condemnation not as a tool of last resort for genuine public works, but as a political veto on private enterprise.
Eminent domain is constitutionally reserved for "public use." Traditionally, that has meant roads, schools, utility corridors, and projects that serve the public and that genuinely require public ownership. Claiming the need for office space might satisfy the letter of state enabling statutes, but the timing of this condemnation is impossible to ignore. Metro is simultaneously pursuing a data center moratorium and aggressive zoning restrictions. To suddenly discover that the exact parcel a data center developer wants must be seized by the city reveals a motive that looks pretextual.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/74370bd9-d6c9-4476-aaaf-831d1dc975c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The practical danger is straightforward enough. If Nashville can seize land because it dislikes a particular industry, other cities will notice. Companies looking to invest billions in infrastructure--often projects that bring significant tax revenue and construction jobs--will factor in the risk that a mayor can simply take the land if politics demand it. That unpredictability chills investment not just in data centers, but in any capital-intensive project that requires long-term certainty.
There is also an awkward contradiction in the policy. Cities across Tennessee and the broader region are actively courting data centers for their economic benefits. Nashville's objection appears rooted partly in neighborhood aesthetics and traffic concerns--legitimate topics for zoning and negotiation--but not for expropriation. If the concern is proximity to the zoo, address it through ordinary land-use authority, setbacks, or negotiated mitigation. If the concern is coding and zoning, rewrite the code. What Metro is doing instead is reaching for one of the most aggressive powers government possesses to ensure that a specific disfavored project simply never happens.
Above all, the precedent cuts both ways. If a mayor can deploy eminent domain to block a data center, another mayor could deploy it to force one in, or to override local objection to any other facility. Condemnation should be a narrow exception, not a flexible political instrument. Nashville's Metro Council may have wrapped this in the language of "office space," but the signal it sends is unmistakable: your property rights extend only as far as the current administration's development preferences allow. Businesses, landowners, and the courts should push back hard before that standard becomes normal.
**Conclusion**
The IIJA's amendments to Section 216 of the Federal Power Act represent one of the most consequential but underreported provisions in the 2021 infrastructure law. By reversing court decisions that had neutered FERC's authority, Congress restored a federal mechanism for siting interstate transmission lines and preserved the power of eminent domain for private developers acting within designated National Corridors. This authority is now being called upon to build the transmission infrastructure necessary to serve a data center economy whose electricity appetite has grown exponentially--connecting generation to load across state lines in ways that individual state regulators could not reliably achieve alone.

In those designated corridors, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) was granted "backstop" authority to issue permits for interstate transmission lines if states failed to act within one year or imposed conditions that did not substantially address the need. Crucially, Section 216(e) authorized permit holders to acquire necessary rights-of-way through federal eminent domain if they could not reach voluntary agreements with landowners. However, this authority proved nearly unusable in practice. In a series of court decisions--most notably the Fourth Circuit's 2009 ruling in Piedmont Environmental Council v. FERC--federal courts interpreted Section 216 narrowly, holding that FERC lacked backstop authority where a state had affirmatively denied a transmission application. Since states could effectively block projects simply by saying "no," FERC's backstop power was rendered largely toothless. Between 2005 and 2021, virtually no major interstate transmission project was successfully sited using the Section 216 framework. The 2021 Fix: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA)--signed into law by President Biden on November 15, 2021 (P.L. 117-58)--was popularly understood as a "$1.2 trillion roads and bridges package." Buried within its provisions, however, was a critically important set of amendments to Section 216 of the FPA that essentially resuscitated and expanded FERC's dormant backstop siting authority. The IIJA amendments accomplished four key things : First, Congress explicitly overrode the Piedmont decision's interpretation. The amended statute now makes clear that FERC may exercise its backstop permitting authority when a state has affirmatively denied a siting application--not merely when a state fails to act within the one-year window. This is the restoration of the backstop power that the courts had stripped away. Second, the amendments expanded the circumstances under which DOE may designate National Corridors, broadening the geographic scope where FERC's authority applies. Third, the IIJA retained the eminent domain power under Section 216(e) but added a "good faith engagement" requirement. FERC must now determine that a permit holder has made genuine, early efforts to engage with landowners and stakeholders before that holder may exercise eminent domain authority to acquire land. | | ---|---|--- Fourth, the amendments clarified and preserved FERC's authority in ways that make the process more predictable for developers seeking to build major interstate transmission projects. The Connection to Data Centers Today While the IIJA's Section 216 amendments were not written with data centers specifically in mind, they laid essential legal groundwork for the massive transmission buildout that is now enabling the data center boom. America's data center industry--particularly hyperscale cloud and AI facilities--has experienced explosive growth. A single modern AI training facility can consume as much electricity as a small city, and developers have been building campuses containing multiple such facilities across Virginia, Texas, Arizona, Ohio, and other states. Regional grids that lacked sufficient transmission capacity to serve this demand faced a fundamental constraint: electrons cannot be transmitted without wires, and crossing state lines historically meant navigating a maze of incompatible permitting regimes. | | ---|---|--- By reviving FERC's backstop authority, the IIJA created a federal pathway for building the large-scale, interstate, high-voltage transmission lines that connect remote generation resources (especially renewable energy in rural areas and offshore wind on the coasts) to the metropolitan and exurban locations where data centers are proliferating. Transmission developers can now pursue federal permits with eminent domain authority when states erect barriers, allowing the grid to expand to meet demand that has grown far beyond what any single state can address on its own. In this sense, the IIJA's Section 216 amendments were a prerequisite condition for the physical infrastructure that supports the modern digital economy. Without robust transmission, there is no reliable power; without reliable power, there are no data centers to train the large language models, stream the content, and store the data that define contemporary life. Who Were the Congressional Sponsors? The IIJA's passage required bipartisan cooperation in an era of deep partisan polarization. The bill's legislative history involved two distinct groups: the Senate bipartisan negotiators who crafted the overall framework, and the House sponsors who advanced the specific vehicle that became law. House Leadership: The formal House vehicle was H.R. 3684, introduced by Representative Peter DeFazio (D-OR), then-Chairman of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure. DeFazio, a longtime champion of federal infrastructure investment, was the named sponsor in the House. The Senate took up the House bill, substituted its negotiated text, and passed it first before returning it to the House for final passage. The Senate Bipartisan Working Group: The breakthrough came from a bipartisan group of senators--sometimes called the "G10" or the "G20" as it expanded--who negotiated the package directly with the White House. The two leaders of this effort were: \- Senator Rob Portman (R-OH) - The Ohio Republican was the lead Republican negotiator and arguably the most visible GOP advocate for the package. \- Senator Kyrsten Sinema (D-AZ) - The Arizona Democrat was the lead Democratic negotiator alongside Portman and was instrumental in keeping the talks alive. The core bipartisan group of senators who announced the initial framework included: \- Bill Cassidy (R-LA) \- Susan Collins (R-ME) \- Joe Manchin (D-WV) \- Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) \- Mitt Romney (R-UT) \- Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) \- Jon Tester (D-MT) \- Mark Warner (D-VA) This group swelled to roughly 20 senators in total as the negotiations proceeded, eventually producing a bill that passed the Senate 69-30 on August 10, 2021. The House then passed the amended bill 228-206 on November 5, 2021, and President Biden signed it into law ten days later. The use of eminent domain to stop a lawful development sets a dangerous precedent, and nowhere is that clearer than in Nashville today. Mayor Freddie O'Connell's decision to seize private property largely to block a DC BLOX data center near the Nashville Zoo deserves scrutiny, because it treats condemnation not as a tool of last resort for genuine public works, but as a political veto on private enterprise. Eminent domain is constitutionally reserved for "public use." Traditionally, that has meant roads, schools, utility corridors, and projects that serve the public and that genuinely require public ownership. Claiming the need for office space might satisfy the letter of state enabling statutes, but the timing of this condemnation is impossible to ignore. Metro is simultaneously pursuing a data center moratorium and aggressive zoning restrictions. To suddenly discover that the exact parcel a data center developer wants must be seized by the city reveals a motive that looks pretextual. | | ---|---|--- The practical danger is straightforward enough. If Nashville can seize land because it dislikes a particular industry, other cities will notice. Companies looking to invest billions in infrastructure--often projects that bring significant tax revenue and construction jobs--will factor in the risk that a mayor can simply take the land if politics demand it. That unpredictability chills investment not just in data centers, but in any capital-intensive project that requires long-term certainty. There is also an awkward contradiction in the policy. Cities across Tennessee and the broader region are actively courting data centers for their economic benefits. Nashville's objection appears rooted partly in neighborhood aesthetics and traffic concerns--legitimate topics for zoning and negotiation--but not for expropriation. If the concern is proximity to the zoo, address it through ordinary land-use authority, setbacks, or negotiated mitigation. If the concern is coding and zoning, rewrite the code. What Metro is doing instead is reaching for one of the most aggressive powers government possesses to ensure that a specific disfavored project simply never happens. Above all, the precedent cuts both ways. If a mayor can deploy eminent domain to block a data center, another mayor could deploy it to force one in, or to override local objection to any other facility. Condemnation should be a narrow exception, not a flexible political instrument. Nashville's Metro Council may have wrapped this in the language of "office space," but the signal it sends is unmistakable: your property rights extend only as far as the current administration's development preferences allow. Businesses, landowners, and the courts should push back hard before that standard becomes normal. Conclusion The IIJA's amendments to Section 216 of the Federal Power Act represent one of the most consequential but underreported provisions in the 2021 infrastructure law. By reversing court decisions that had neutered FERC's authority, Congress restored a federal mechanism for siting interstate transmission lines and preserved the power of eminent domain for private developers acting within designated National Corridors. This authority is now being called upon to build the transmission infrastructure necessary to serve a data center economy whose electricity appetite has grown exponentially--connecting generation to load across state lines in ways that individual state regulators could not reliably achieve alone. | | ---|---|--- Thanks for reading! **Peter, it’s John James. **
I wanted to introduce myself. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. _I promise I will not waste your time._

clean_body: I’m a combat veteran and a father. I hope you will read this.| | | | | Peter, it’s John James. I wanted to introduce myself. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. I promise I will not waste your time. I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted. I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, I would live it. Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army. During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud. After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician... I saw the Democrats destroying our country, and I knew my service to this great nation wasn’t over yet. Everybody told me running for office isn’t easy, but my heart was telling me it was the right thing to do. I won my election, with the help of President Trump, and started delivering results for my new constituents. Then, in 2023, when the Establishment tried to move on from Trump and being MAGA was seen as risky or politically inconvenient, I was among the first in Michigan to endorse President Trump for 2024. Loyalty isn’t a talking point to me; it’s the only way I know how to operate. My dedication to this country, my loyalty towards my constituents, and my desire to see the greatest nation on earth excel are part of the reasons why I’m now emailing you, but they’re not my #1 reason why... These three kids are the reason why I’m sending this message to you, as a Republican and father running to be the next governor of Michigan Having my own family taught me more lessons than I could list, and it was the one thing being in the U.S. Army didn’t prepare me for. But it also awoke in me a desire to do EVERYTHING and ANYTHING I can to ensure my kids have bright futures. My family means everything to me, and Michigan is our home; that’s why I will fight like my life depends on it to save this state and win this November. I’m under no illusions; I know this election will be one of the toughest challenges I’ve faced in my entire life, but after everything I’ve done in my service, it’s nothing I can’t handle. Unfortunately, the one thing I can’t directly control is spending, and the Democrats will do everything in their power to stop my campaign from making it to the ballot box this November. Nothing can stop us from saving this country if we stand together. Today, I’m asking you to make a small-dollar gift of $10, $25, $50 or ANYTHING you can spare to fuel my campaign’s fight as we approach our upcoming November 3rd election. Thank you for taking the time to read my message. I hope to hear from you in the days to come. Derek, Donald Trump would rather shut down the Kennedy Center than let it stand without his name on it. It's not just absurd. It's destructive of a great cultural institution— and absurd — the president of the United States, spending his time and energy scheming over whether his name goes on a memorial named for an assassinated president, while one of the nation's great cultural institutions sits closed because of it. _If the President can't put his name on it, he is willing to close it or destroy it._ He cares more about branding our institutions in his image than he does preserving them for all of us. Congress allocated $257 million to repair the Kennedy Center. It should insist that work be done properly — not held hostage until Trump's name goes back on the building. Congress could stop this in a heartbeat if it wanted to. My colleagues have pushed for bipartisan legislation — Democrats and Republicans together — to protect the Kennedy Center, and memorials like it, from being torn down without Congress's consent. **[_Will you add your name in support of this fight to protect the Kennedy Center and stop Trump from treating our institutions like his personal property?_](https://act.adamschiff.com/signup/aschiff_email_100126_kennedycenterpetition?t=10&refcode=aschiff_email_100126_kennedycenterpetition&akid=10626%2E5257348%2E-FR8kz)** | | [ADD YOUR NAME→](https://act.adamschiff.com/signup/aschiff_email_100126_kennedycenterpetition?t=11&refcode=aschiff_email_100126_kennedycenterpetition&akid=10626%2E5257348%2E-FR8kz)

We hit our goals for September, and that means we’re still on track to raise what we need to meet all of our commitments ahead of the election next month.

Because yesterday, Pete Hegseth gave what he clearly thought was his “Patton” speech. You know the one.

Peter, we wish we could take some time off to give you a break after an important fundraising deadline. Normally, we would. But the truth is, there’s no time. We have to keep up the pressure, because we can’t fall short.

body:
Let’s finish strong.

I could not be more grateful. When I woke up this morning to check our fundraising numbers, I saw that we didn’t just hit last night’s End-of-Quarter goal. **We blew right past it.** When our fundraising data goes public, everyone is going to see just how strong this incredible grassroots movement is — and that’s all because of people like you. **Thank you.** But as much as I love to celebrate the small victories, we have to keep our eye on the prize. This is our last full month on the campaign trail — and the House majority is swinging in the balance. Carmela Conroy, in her own words, called on Congress to “dismantle and behead” the Department of Homeland Security.Now she’s insisting she didn’t say it. (Does she not remember?!) But her dishonesty isn’t the main issue – the substance behind those words matters even more.DHS is responsible for securing our border and enforcing our immigration laws. It also includes the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) that provides aid to areas stricken by wildfires and other natural disasters.And she wants to behead it. You can imagine how people in Washington, D.C. react to that insulting, irresponsible language. Thankfully, I am working to make sure that our federal aid request is on track.(In addition to beheading DHS, Conroy also proposed a bizarre plan – and I’m not making this up – to empty illegal immigrant detention centers so illegal aliens could help fund Social Security, saying illegals “...all contribute to it.”)That isn't a minor policy disagreement. And it isn't something voters should have to discover by watching an old clip after being told it never happened.[Carmela said it. The tape shows it.](https://us.list-manage.com/iZVAK7bZGf8?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)I walked out of our last debate just shaking my head. Where does she get these ideas? When we are asking the federal government for disaster relief, I can only describe her actions as undiplomatic, to say the least.-Michael

name: Biancoforsheriff
subject: Sacramento just targeted me — and only me
body:
Must read

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/f8pmj7VIOil?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
| |

Friends,

**Governor Newsom just signed SB 1379.**
This bill was authored by DSA State Sen. Sabrina Cervantes. Now she and Sacramento have used state power to strip me of an office the voters of Riverside County elected me to serve.
I was elected Sheriff and public Coroner. That is how 48 of California’s 58 counties still operate. One person. One department. Local control.SB 1379 does not apply to those other 57 counties. It targets Riverside County. **It targets me**.
---
| | | | | [Support Bianco](https://us.list-manage.com/E4XGstGcNgV?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
---
| |
The Democrat-majority Board of Supervisors now has to appoint a separate official and stand up an entirely new department — staff, building, bureaucracy — while the county is already staring at a nearly $70 million deficit. Taxpayers will pay for a political hit job.This is not reform. **This is political weaponization**.
The same Democrat supervisors already shorted my department by $125 million. That is not “oversight.” **This is defund the police**.
Look at the pattern.They defunded the Sheriff’s Office. They passed a law to stop sheriffs from examining ballots that are the subject of a criminal investigation. The California Supreme Court then piled on. Now they carve the Coroner’s Office away from the only county they decided to single out.
This is what one-party rule looks like when it cannot beat you at the ballot box: change the rules. Isolate one official.
**Stand with me. Contribute what you can. Help me fight this.**

Sheriff Chad Bianco
Riverside County

# [#]
Hi friend,

I wanted to take a moment and say thank you!

I know that you received a lot of emails this past week, so I can’t thank you enough for all your support leading up to our final FEC deadline before Election Day.

Our campaign is powered by folks chipping in whenever they can, especially as we approach these important deadlines.

Seeing all this support, I am confident we have the momentum needed to keep NY-16 blue and take back control of the House this November.

We’re on the path to bring common sense back to Washington and hold the Trump Administration accountable for all the chaos they caused. With just over one month before Election Day, I am grateful to have you with me in this final stretch.

Thank you again for all your support,

George

Peter,

Angry Leftists tried for two years to**EXCUSE Luigi Mangione 's political violence... **to claim he was "fighting corporate greed" and some kind of "American hero."

You and I always knew what he was, and now he's admitted it:

_**He 's nothing more than a cold-blooded killer.**_

Last month, Mangione stood up in federal court and told the truth. He pleaded guilty to stalking Brian Thompson. He admitted, in his own words, that he shot him and that Thompson died. He now faces life in prison.

Brian Thompson was a husband and a father of two. The man was gunned down on a Manhattan sidewalk for the crime of running a successful company.

But here's the issue, Peter:

**The radical collectivist ideology that bent over backwards to LIONIZE him for being a violent murderer is still VERY much alive.**

Because that's what these dehumanizing ideologues teach young people: that it's somehow **_MORAL_ to violently punish someone simply for being successful.**

I'm Jennifer Anju Grossman, CEO of The Atlas Society. Ayn Rand spent her life warning the West what happens when a culture stops honoring achievement and starts resenting it.

She had a name for what drives someone to cheer a murderer because the victim was successful: envy, "the hatred of the good for being good."

Ayn Rand offered a radical alternative: that **achievement is not a crime...** and **political disagreement is NOT an excuse** to commit violence.

At the Atlas Society, **we 're fighting to reach young people BEFORE their resentments curdle into radicalism and violence.**

Engage young people with Ayn Rand's fierce advocacy for reason, individualism, and freedom to INSPIRE the next generation.
